argentina.text: The world's sixth-largest wine producer in 2025, with vine cuttings first brought to Santiago del Estero in the 1550s. Malbec is the most planted grape at 24%, followed by Cereza and Bonarda. Its provinces include Mendoza, San Juan and Río Negro.

argentina/25-de-mayo.text: A wine area in San Juan.

argentina/avellaneda.text: A wine area in Río Negro, one of Argentina's wine-producing provinces. Malbec leads plantings at 33%, followed by Merlot (12%) and Pinot Noir (8%).

argentina/chubut.text: A province in Argentine wine country whose wine areas include El Hoyo and Trevelin.

argentina/godoy-cruz.text: A wine area in Mendoza, part of the metropolitan area of the city of Mendoza.

cite.name: Wikipedia, Godoy Cruz, Mendoza

argentina/mendoza.text: Argentina's dominant wine region, making around three-quarters of the country's wine. Vineyards sit high in the eastern foothills of the Andes, and Malbec is the leading grape.

argentina/san-juan.text: An Argentine province and one of the country's main wine regions, containing 25 de Mayo, Albardón, Calingasta, Iglesia, Pocito, Zonda and others. Cereza leads plantings at 34%, followed by Malbec (10%) and Syrah (7%).

argentina/santa-lucia.text: A wine area in San Juan. Cereza dominates plantings at 55%, followed by Bonarda (7%) and Malbec (5%).

australia.text: One of the world's largest wine exporters, sending about 613 million of its roughly 1.1 billion liters abroad in 2025. Wine is made in every state, and South Australia makes about half. Shiraz is the most planted grape at 30 percent, then Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay.

cite.name: Wine Australia, National Vintage Report 2025

australia/albany.text: A subregion of Great Southern in Western Australia, around the south coast town of Albany.

australia/barossa-valley.text: A warm region about 35 miles northeast of Adelaide, in the Barossa zone of South Australia, settled in the 1840s by English and German settlers. Its warm, dry summers gave very ripe grapes and an early fortified wine industry. Shiraz is 65 percent of plantings, then Cabernet Sauvignon at 14 percent.

australia/canberra-district.text: A cool-climate region around Canberra, in the Southern New South Wales zone, with Murrumbateman, Yass and Bungendore among its key places. Lower, inland parts near Yass are warmer than the high ground near Bungendore. Shiraz is 32 percent of plantings, then Cabernet Sauvignon at 14 and Riesling at 12.

australia/central-western-australia.text: A zone in Western Australia with no regions registered inside it and only a few scattered vineyards.

cite.name: Tille, Stuart-Street and Gardiner, Geology, soils and climate of Western Australia's wine regions, DPIRD Bulletin 4925 (2022)

australia/far-north.text: A South Australian zone. The Southern Flinders Ranges lie inside it. South Australia as a whole crushes about half of all Australian wine grapes.

cite.name: Wine Australia, National Vintage Report 2025

australia/geographe.text: A region in the South West Australia zone of Western Australia. Shiraz leads plantings at 21 percent, followed by Sauvignon Blanc (19), Chardonnay (17), Cabernet Sauvignon (13) and Semillon (11).

australia/gippsland.text: A large Victorian zone where Pinot Noir leads plantings at 38 percent, followed by Chardonnay (20) and Shiraz (18).

australia/glenrowan.text: A region in the North East Victoria zone, between Benalla and Wangaratta. Shiraz and Cabernet Sauvignon are each 32 percent of plantings.

australia/lower-murray.text: A South Australian zone containing the Riverland region. South Australia as a whole crushes about half of Australia's wine grapes.

cite.name: Wine Australia, National Vintage Report 2025

australia/margaret-river.text: A region in southwest Western Australia, in the South West Australia area, and the most maritime-influenced of the major Australian regions, with a Mediterranean pattern of rainfall. Cabernet Sauvignon is 26 percent of plantings, then Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz and Semillon.

australia/mclaren-vale.text: A South Australian region in the Fleurieu area. Shiraz is 57 percent of plantings, with Cabernet Sauvignon at 18 percent and Grenache at 6 percent.

australia/mornington-peninsula.text: A cool-climate region south of Melbourne in Victoria's Port Phillip area, focused on Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and Pinot Gris too. Pinot Noir is 55 percent of plantings.

australia/mount-lofty-ranges.text: A South Australian zone containing Adelaide Hills, Adelaide Plains and Clare Valley. South Australia as a whole crushes about half of Australia's wine grapes.

cite.name: Wine Australia, National Vintage Report 2025

australia/mudgee.text: A New South Wales region in the Central Ranges zone. It grows mostly red grapes, led by Shiraz and Cabernet Sauvignon, with Chardonnay close behind.

australia/murray-darling.text: A large wine region straddling the Murray River, partly in the Big Rivers zone of New South Wales and partly in the North West Victoria zone.

australia/north-west-victoria.text: A zone in northwest Victoria along the Murray River. Its two regions, Murray Darling and Swan Hill, both cross the river into New South Wales.

australia/northern-rivers.text: A New South Wales zone of about 16,700 square miles, with Hastings River as its one region. It has only about 100 acres of vines, led by Semillon at 29 percent.

australia/riverina.text: A large irrigated region in the Big Rivers zone of New South Wales, centered on Griffith and relying heavily on the Murrumbidgee Irrigation Area. Shiraz and Chardonnay lead the plantings.

australia/south-australia.text: The state that makes about half of all Australian wine. Its range runs from Riesling in Clare Valley to big, full-bodied Shiraz in Barossa Valley.

australia/southern-flinders-ranges.text: A region in the Far North zone of South Australia, east and northeast of Port Pirie. South Australia makes about half of all Australian wine.

australia/swan-hill.text: A region spanning the Murray River in Victoria and New South Wales, with almost all vineyards irrigated from the river. Its fruity Shiraz and Chardonnay are generally best drunk within about two years of vintage.

cite.name: Wine Australia, Swan Hill regional profile

australia/tasmania.text: Pinot Noir is almost half of plantings, followed by Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc.

australia/west-australian-south-east-coa.text: A zone along the south coast of Western Australia, around Ravensthorpe and Esperance.

australia/western-australia.text: Western Australia makes less than 5% of Australia's wine.

austria.text: A country of mostly dry white wine, led by Grüner Veltliner at 33 percent of vines. About 30 percent of wine is red, mainly from Zweigelt and Blaufränkisch. Sweet wines come from around Neusiedler See.

austria/eisenberg.text: A wine area in Burgenland, Austria, whose DAC wine is red Blaufränkisch, with Welschriesling also allowed for village and single-vineyard wines.

cite.name: Austrian Ministry of Agriculture, Eisenberg DAC um Welschriesling erweitert (DAC-Verordnung Eisenberg, in force 18 Sep 2024)

austria/kamptal.text: A wine area in Niederösterreich (Lower Austria), Austria, whose Kamptal DAC wine is white, from Grüner Veltliner and Riesling, joined from the 2024 vintage by Chardonnay, Weissburgunder and Grauburgunder. Grüner Veltliner covers 55 percent of its vineyards and Riesling 10, with Zweigelt also planted.

cite.name: Austrian Ministry of Agriculture, Kamptal DAC neu ab Jahrgang 2024 (DAC-Verordnung Kamptal, BGBl. II Nr. 250/2024)

austria/kremstal.text: A wine area in Niederösterreich (Lower Austria), Austria, whose DAC wines are Grüner Veltliner or Riesling. The standard wines must not be dominated by botrytis, while Reserve wines may show a delicate touch of botrytis and oak.

cite.name: Produktspezifikation Kremstal DAC (Austrian Ministry of Agriculture, 2022)

austria/leithaberg.text: A wine area in Burgenland, Austria, whose DAC covers red wine from Blaufränkisch and white wine from Chardonnay, Grüner Veltliner, Neuburger and Weissburgunder. Blaufränkisch is the most planted grape at 21 percent, followed by Grüner Veltliner at 14.

austria/neusiedlersee.text: A wine area in Burgenland, Austria, where Zweigelt is the most planted grape at 24 percent, ahead of Grüner Veltliner, Welschriesling and Blaufränkisch. Its DAC covers dry reds based on Zweigelt and, since 2020, sweet wines.

austria/traisental.text: A wine district in Niederösterreich (Lower Austria), Austria, south of Krems. Grüner Veltliner dominates at 64 percent. Traisental DAC covers Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.

austria/wachau.text: A wine region in Niederösterreich (Lower Austria), on the Danube west of Vienna, known for dry Riesling and Grüner Veltliner. Its growers' association has its own three-level system for dry wines, from Steinfeder, up to 11.5 percent alcohol, to Smaragd. Grüner Veltliner covers 64 percent of vines.

chile/aconcagua.text: One of Chile's six wine regions, covering all vineyards in the Valparaíso Region. It includes Casablanca, San Antonio and Aconcagua Valleys.

cite.name: Decreto 464 (1994), Zonificación vitícola, consolidated text, Servicio Agrícola y Ganadero

chile/bio-bio-valley.text: A subregion of Southern Chile, one of the six wine regions of Chile, alongside the Itata and Malleco valleys.

chile/elqui-valley.text: A northern Chilean valley in the Coquimbo region, at the southern end of the Atacama Desert, running from the Pacific to the Andes. It is known for table grapes and pisco.

chile/itata-valley.text: A subregion of Southern Chile, one of Chile's six wine regions, alongside the Bío Bío and Malleco valleys.

chile/malleco-valley.text: A subregion of Southern Chile, one of Chile's six wine regions. The South runs from the Ñuble and Biobío regions to the province of Malleco in Araucanía, and is made up of three subregions: the Itata, Bío Bío and Malleco valleys.

chile/maule-valley.text: A subregion at the southern end of Chile's Central Valley. Cabernet Sauvignon covers 28 percent of vines, followed by Sauvignon Blanc at 14 percent and País at 11 percent.

chile/southern-chile.text: One of Chile's six wine regions, running from the Ñuble and Biobío regions to the province of Malleco in Araucanía. It has three subregions: Itata, Bío-Bío and Malleco Valleys.

cite.name: Decreto 464 de 1994, Zonificación vitícola (Ministerio de Agricultura, Chile), as amended by Decreto 27 de 2024

france/alsace-grand-cru.text: Alsace's grand cru tier, first recognized in 1975 and now 51 named vineyards, each its own AOC. Their rules are stricter than Alsace AOC's, including a base yield of 50 hectoliters per hectare for white wine.

cite.name: Cahier des charges de l'AOC Alsace grand cru, homologué par l'arrêté du 4 juillet 2025 (BO n°29 du 17 juillet 2025)

france/alsace-grand-cru-altenberg-de-ber.text: An Alsace Grand Cru vineyard in Bergheim. Its white wines are either a single variety of Riesling, Gewürztraminer or Pinot Gris, or a blend led by Riesling with Gewürztraminer and Pinot Gris. Chasselas, the three Muscats, Pinot Blanc and Pinot Noir may make up a small part of a blend, but only from vines planted before 2005.

france/alsace-grand-cru-kaefferkopf.text: An Alsace Grand Cru vineyard in Ammerschwihr. Its white wines are either a single variety of Gewürztraminer, Riesling or Pinot Gris, or a blend led by Gewürztraminer with Riesling. Pinot Gris and the three Muscats may play smaller roles in a blend.

france/alsace-grand-cru-zotzenberg.text: An Alsace Grand Cru vineyard in Mittelbergheim. Its wines can be made from four grapes, Riesling, Gewürztraminer, Pinot Gris and Sylvaner, but not the Muscats. Each wine is made from one grape alone.

france/ambonnay.text: A cru village in the Montagne de Reims, a Champagne area where soils are chalk-based and Pinot Noir is the main grape. Champagne's rules allow sparkling wine from Pinot Noir, Meunier and Chardonnay, plus Arbane, Petit Meslier, Pinot Blanc and Pinot Gris, with the new variety Voltis allowed on up to 5 percent of a grower's vines.

cite.name: Cahier des charges de l’appellation d'origine contrôlée Champagne, homologué par l'arrêté du 31 juillet 2025 (AGRT2518163A) - BO n°32 du 7 août 2025

france/anjou.text: A Loire Valley appellation near the city of Angers, part of the Middle Loire with Saumur and Touraine. Rules allow still white and red wine and sparkling white and rosé. Whites rest mainly on Chenin Blanc and reds on Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon, with Grolleau, Gamay and Chardonnay among the other grapes allowed.

france/arbois.text: A Jura appellation, in the cool climate region between Burgundy and Switzerland, for wine made from Savagnin Blanc, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Poulsard and Trousseau. Its rules also allow vin jaune and vin de paille. Pupillin is among its communes.

france/avenay-val-dor.text: A Champagne village. Champagne's rules allow sparkling wine from Pinot Noir, Meunier and Chardonnay, plus Arbane, Petit Meslier, Pinot Blanc and Pinot Gris, with the new variety Voltis allowed on up to 5 percent of a grower's vines.

cite.name: Cahier des charges de l’appellation d'origine contrôlée Champagne, homologué par l'arrêté du 31 juillet 2025 (AGRT2518163A) - BO n°32 du 7 août 2025

france/avize.text: A cru village in the Côte des Blancs, an area of Champagne vineyards named for its grape, where Chardonnay is grown above all and many champagnes are blanc de blancs, from white grapes only.

france/bandol.text: A Provence appellation around Bandol, Le Castellet and Sanary-sur-Mer for red, rosé and white wine. Reds must be 50 to 95 percent Mourvèdre, with Grenache and Cinsault as the other main grapes. Whites are based on Clairette, Bourboulenc and Ugni Blanc.

france/banyuls.text: A fortified vin doux naturel from terraced slopes of the Catalan Pyrenees in Roussillon, in Languedoc-Roussillon near the Spanish border. Fermentation is stopped by adding alcohol. Its main allowed grapes are Grenache (red, white and gray), Macabeu and Tourbat.

france/banyuls-grand-cru.text: A Languedoc-Roussillon vin doux naturel appellation for red wine, covering Banyuls-sur-Mer, Cerbère, Collioure and Port-Vendres. Grenache must make up at least 75 percent of the vines, and the wines are aged at least 30 months in wood.

cite.name: INAO, Banyuls grand cru product sheet

france/bearn.text: A South West France appellation in three separate sectors: around Salies-de-Béarn and Bellocq in the west, south and west of Pau, and in a loop of the Adour to the northeast. Its rules allow Tannat, Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon, along with Petit Manseng, Gros Manseng and Raffiat de Moncade.

france/beaujolais.text: A French appellation between Mâcon and Lyon, best known for light-bodied red wine from Gamay, a thin-skinned, low-tannin grape. White, made only from Chardonnay, is about 4 percent of production. Crus within it include Morgon, Fleurie, Moulin-à-Vent and Brouilly.

france/beaumes-de-venise.text: A southern Rhône Valley appellation for red wine only, recognized in 2005, made mainly from Grenache with at least 20 percent Syrah. The village also gives its name to Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise, a separate appellation for sweet fortified vin doux naturel.

cite.name: Cahier des charges de l'AOC Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise, homologué par arrêté du 11 mars 2021 (BO du 18 mars 2021)

france/beaumont-sur-vesle.text: A cru village in the Montagne de Reims, a Champagne area where soils are chalk-based and Pinot Noir is the main grape. Champagne's rules allow sparkling wine from Pinot Noir, Meunier and Chardonnay, plus Arbane, Petit Meslier, Pinot Blanc and Pinot Gris, with the new variety Voltis allowed on up to 5 percent of a grower's vines.

cite.name: Cahier des charges de l'AOC Champagne, homologué par l'arrêté du 31 juillet 2025 (BO agri du 7 août 2025)

france/bergeres-les-vertus.text: A Champagne village. Champagne's rules allow sparkling wine from Pinot Noir, Meunier and Chardonnay, plus Arbane, Petit Meslier, Pinot Blanc and Pinot Gris, with the new variety Voltis allowed on up to 5 percent of a grower's vines.

cite.name: Cahier des charges de l'AOC Champagne, homologué par l'arrêté du 31 juillet 2025 (BO agri du 7 août 2025)

france/bezannes.text: A village in the Champagne area. Champagne's rules allow sparkling wine from Pinot Noir, Meunier and Chardonnay, plus Arbane, Petit Meslier, Pinot Blanc and Pinot Gris, with the new variety Voltis allowed on up to 5 percent of a grower's vines.

cite.name: Cahier des charges de l'AOC Champagne, homologué par l'arrêté du 31 juillet 2025 (BO agri du 7 août 2025)

france/billy-le-grand.text: A village within Champagne. Champagne's rules allow sparkling wine from Pinot Noir, Meunier and Chardonnay, plus Arbane, Petit Meslier, Pinot Blanc and Pinot Gris, with the new variety Voltis allowed on up to 5 percent of a grower's vines.

cite.name: Cahier des charges de l'AOC Champagne, homologué par l'arrêté du 31 juillet 2025 (BO agri du 7 août 2025)

france/blagny.text: A Côte de Beaune appellation for red wine from Pinot Noir, from vineyards in Meursault and Puligny-Montrachet. Seven climats there may be labeled premier cru.

france/blaye-cotes-de-bordeaux.text: A Right Bank Bordeaux appellation, made as Côtes de Bordeaux with the Blaye name added, for red and dry white wine. Its reds come from Merlot, the Cabernets, Cot, Carmenère and Petit Verdot, and its whites mainly from Sauvignon, Sauvignon Gris, Sémillon and Muscadelle.

cite.name: Cahier des charges de l'AOC Côtes de Bordeaux, homologué par arrêté du 26 octobre 2021 (BO du 11 novembre 2021)

france/bordeaux-bordeaux-superieur.text: A grouping within Bordeaux that holds the Bordeaux Supérieur appellation. Bordeaux's rules allow Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cot, Carmenère and Petit Verdot for red, plus Sauvignon, Sémillon and Muscadelle. The Gironde area grows mostly Merlot (58 percent) and Cabernet Sauvignon (20).

france/bordeaux-superieur.text: A Bordeaux appellation within the Bordeaux & Bordeaux Supérieur group. Its rules allow Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Cot, Carmenère and Petit Verdot, plus Sémillon, Sauvignon and Muscadelle. The Gironde grows mostly Merlot (58 percent) and Cabernet Sauvignon (20).

france/bourgogne.text: A Burgundy appellation spread across many communes, including Aloxe-Corton, Ancey and Augy. Its rules allow Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Pinot Blanc and Pinot Gris, with César as a minor grape only in the Yonne and Gamay only in reds from the Beaujolais crus.

france/bourgogne-mousseux.text: A Burgundy appellation for red sparkling wine. Its rules allow Pinot Noir and Gamay, plus César in the Yonne, with Aligoté, Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc also allowed as minor grapes.

france/bouzeron.text: A white wine appellation in the Côte Chalonnaise, Burgundy, made from Aligoté. It is the only communal-level Burgundy appellation for Aligoté. Elsewhere in Burgundy, Aligoté goes into regional appellations such as Bourgogne Aligoté and Coteaux Bourguignons.

cite.name: Cahier des charges de l'AOC Coteaux Bourguignons, homologué par l'arrêté du 12 janvier 2024 (BO n°4 du 25 janvier 2024)

france/bouzy.text: A cru village in the Montagne de Reims, a Champagne sub-region where soils are chalk-based and Pinot Noir is the main grape. Champagne's rules allow sparkling wine from Pinot Noir, Meunier and Chardonnay, plus Arbane, Petit Meslier, Pinot Blanc, Pinot Gris and Chardonnay Rose, with up to 5 percent Voltis.

cite.name: Cahier des charges de l'AOC Champagne, homologué par l'arrêté du 31 juillet 2025 (BO n°32 du 7 août 2025)

france/cabardes.text: A Languedoc-Roussillon appellation for red and rosé wine, made from grapes such as Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah, Grenache and Cabernet Franc. It became an AOC only in 1999.

france/cabernet-d-anjou.text: A Loire Valley appellation for still rosé wine with some sweetness, made from Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon.

france/cabernet-de-saumur.text: A Loire Valley appellation for still rosé wine, made from Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon.

france/cahors.text: A South West France appellation for red wine only, built on Malbec, known locally as Cot or Auxerrois. Malbec must make up at least 70% of the blend, with Merlot and Tannat allowed in smaller roles.

france/cerons.text: A Bordeaux appellation on the Left Bank covering Cérons, Illats and Podensac, for sweet white wine only. Its wines are made from Sémillon, Sauvignon Blanc, Sauvignon Gris and Muscadelle.

france/champagne.text: An appellation in northeast France for sparkling wine, made by secondary fermentation in the bottle. Pinot Noir, Meunier and Chardonnay make almost all of it, with small amounts of Pinot Blanc, Pinot Gris, Arbane and Petit Meslier. It became linked with royalty and luxury.

france/chassagne-montrachet.text: A Côte de Beaune village appellation making mostly white wine from Chardonnay, with a smaller share of red from Pinot Noir.

france/chateau-chalon.text: A Jura appellation reserved for vin jaune ("yellow wine"), a still white made from Savagnin. Current rules also allow small shares of Enfariné and Gringet on trial.

france/chinon.text: A Touraine appellation in the Loire Valley making mostly red wine from Cabernet Franc, with smaller amounts of rosé and a little white from Chenin Blanc.

france/clairette-de-die.text: A Rhône Valley appellation for sparkling white wine. Most is labeled méthode ancestrale, mainly from Muscat à Petits Grains and finished in bottle from partly fermented must, so it is low in alcohol and sweet. A traditional-method wine is also made from Clairette alone.

france/clairette-du-languedoc.text: A Languedoc-Roussillon appellation for white wine made only from Clairette. The rules allow still white wine and a white vin de liqueur.

france/coligny.text: A cru village of Champagne, whose wider appellation makes quality sparkling wine. Champagne's rules allow Chardonnay, Meunier and Pinot Noir, along with Arbane, Petit Meslier, Pinot Blanc, Pinot Gris and Chardonnay Rose.

cite.name: Cahier des charges de l'AOC Champagne, homologué par l'arrêté du 31 juillet 2025

france/collioure.text: A Roussillon appellation within Languedoc-Roussillon, making red, rosé and white wines. Reds are based on Grenache, Mourvèdre, Syrah and Carignan, and whites on Grenache Blanc, Grenache Gris, Macabeu, Marsanne, Roussanne, Tourbat and Vermentino. Its boundaries match Banyuls, whose grapes go into fortified wines.

france/corbieres.text: Corbières has a varied geology, but its vineyards lie mostly on stony, well-drained clay-limestone soils.

france/corton.text: A large Grand Cru hill in the Côte de Beaune, shared by Aloxe-Corton, Pernand-Vergelesses and Ladoix, making red and white wine. Reds use Pinot Noir and whites use Chardonnay. Red labels may add a climat name, as in Corton Les Bressandes.

france/costieres-de-nimes.text: A Rhône Valley appellation between Nîmes and the western Rhône delta, in the Gard. Its wines resemble Rhône wines more than Languedoc ones. Reds and rosés are based on Grenache, Mourvèdre and Syrah, and whites on Grenache Blanc, Marsanne and Roussanne.

france/cote-de-beaune.text: The southern part of the Côte d'Or limestone ridge, about 15 miles long. Reds continue from the Côte de Nuits but are lighter and more perfumed. Farther south lie great white names like Meursault and Chassagne-Montrachet.

france/cote-de-beaune-villages.text: A Côte de Beaune appellation for red wine only, from a long list of villages, including Meursault, Puligny-Montrachet, Pernand-Vergelesses and Chorey-lès-Beaune. Its wine is based on Pinot Noir.

cite.name: INAO, fiche produit AOP Côte de Beaune-Villages, and the INAO list of its 16 communes

france/cote-de-brouilly.text: A Beaujolais appellation for Gamay in four communes: Cercié, Odenas, Quincié-en-Beaujolais and Saint-Lager. Beaujolais reds are generally Gamay.

france/cote-de-nuits.text: The northern part of the Côte d'Or, from Dijon to just south of Nuits-Saint-Georges. It is best known for reds made from Pinot Noir. Six of its communes produce Grand Cru wines.

france/coteaux-bourguignons.text: A regional appellation for red, white and rosé wine from across Burgundy and Beaujolais. The name means "Burgundian hills". Grapes include Gamay, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Aligoté.

france/coteaux-d-ancenis.text: A Loire Valley appellation for white, red and rosé wine. Whites are made only from Pinot Gris, and reds and rosés from Gamay with Cabernet Franc as a minor grape.

france/coteaux-du-lyonnais.text: An appellation on the slopes of the Monts du Lyonnais, west of Lyon, between the Beaujolais and Rhône Valley vineyards. Reds and rosés are made from Gamay, and whites from Chardonnay and Aligoté.

france/coteaux-varois-en-provence.text: A Provence appellation for red, rosé and white wine. Reds and rosés are led by Cinsault, Grenache, Mourvèdre and Syrah, and whites draw on Clairette, Grenache Blanc, Sémillon, Ugni Blanc and Vermentino.

france/cotes-de-bordeaux.text: A large Bordeaux-area appellation for red wine from grapes such as Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon and Malbec. White wine is made only under the Blaye, Francs and Sainte-Foy names.

france/cotes-de-bourg.text: A Right Bank Bordeaux appellation around Bourg-sur-Gironde, on the right bank of the Dordogne and the Gironde, north of Bordeaux. Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon and Cot are among the grapes allowed.

france/cotes-de-duras.text: A South West France appellation for red, white and rosé wine, in Lot-et-Garonne, just east of the Bordeaux border. Grapes allowed include Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon, Sémillon and Muscadelle.

france/cotes-du-forez.text: A Loire Valley appellation whose wine is made only from Gamay. It covers a group of communes including Montbrison, Boën-sur-Lignon and Champdieu. Its vineyards are the farthest upstream in the Loire Valley.

france/cotes-du-jura.text: A Jura appellation for white, red and rosé wine, which may also be labeled vin jaune or vin de paille. Grapes include Savagnin, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Poulsard and Trousseau, and its communes include Arbois and Baume-les-Messieurs. Jura is a cool climate region between Burgundy and Switzerland.

france/cotes-du-marmandais.text: A South West France appellation around Marmande, on both banks of the Garonne just southeast of Entre-Deux-Mers, outside the Bordeaux region. It became an AOC in 1990. Its main allowed grapes are Sauvignon, Sauvignon Gris, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Cabernet Franc.

france/cotes-du-rhone-villages.text: A Rhône Valley appellation listed under the Southern Rhône, usable in a limited part of the region. Its label may add one of 21 named places, such as Séguret, Sablet or Plan de Dieu.

france/cotes-du-roussillon.text: A Roussillon appellation in Languedoc-Roussillon, for red, rosé and white wine.

cite.name: Cahier des charges de l'AOP Côtes du Roussillon homologué par arrêté du 22 mars 2022 publié au JORF du 29 mars 2022 - B.O. n°14 du 31 mars 2022

france/cramant.text: A cru village in the Côte des Blancs, an area of Champagne vineyards where Chardonnay is grown above all and many champagnes are blanc de blancs, from white grapes only.

france/cremant-d-alsace.text: Alsace's sparkling wine, made like champagne and recognized as an AOC in 1976. It is made from Pinot Blanc, Pinot Gris, Pinot Noir, Riesling, Auxerrois and Chardonnay, and the rosé from Pinot Noir only.

france/crozes-hermitage.text: A Northern Rhône appellation whose wines are mostly red, made from Syrah. Some white wine is made from Marsanne and Roussanne.

france/drome.text: An IGP for wines of the Drôme. Across all the Drôme's vineyards, whatever their appellation, Grenache (38%) and Syrah (33%) are planted most, with Muscat Blanc, Carignan and Merlot far behind.

france/faugeres.text: A Languedoc appellation in the foothills of the Massif Central north of Béziers. Its red and rosé wines are made from Grenache, Syrah, Mourvèdre and Lledoner Pelut, with Carignan required at 10 to 40 percent of a grower's vines. Its whites are made from Marsanne, Roussanne, Vermentino and Grenache Blanc.

france/fiefs-vendeens.text: A Loire Valley appellation in the Vendée for red, rosé and white wine. Pinot Noir, Négrette and Cabernet Franc are the main red grapes, Pinot Noir and Gamay lead the rosés, and the whites are made mainly from Chenin, with some Chardonnay.

france/gigondas.text: A southern Rhône appellation in the commune of Gigondas, mainly for red wine from Grenache, with a little rosé. White wine was added. The red is a wine for ageing.

france/grand-auxerrois.text: A Burgundy area in the Yonne. Its village appellations are Saint-Bris, Vézelay and Irancy, and it also has regional Bourgogne names such as Bourgogne Côtes d'Auxerre and Bourgogne Tonnerre.

cite.name: Bourgogne Wines (BIVB), Chablis and Grand Auxerrois

france/graves-de-vayres.text: A Bordeaux appellation for red and white wine from two communes, Vayres and Arveyres, on the left bank of the Dordogne in the Entre-Deux-Mers area, though outside the Entre-Deux-Mers appellation. Reds use Merlot and Cabernets, whites use Sauvignon, Sémillon and Muscadelle.

france/graves-superieures.text: A Left Bank Bordeaux name for sweet white wine, based on Sémillon with Sauvignon and Muscadelle. These wines now come under the Graves appellation, and the Graves supérieures name may be used only until the 2028 harvest.

france/grignan-les-adhemar.text: A Rhône Valley appellation in the Drôme for red, rosé and white wine. Reds are based on Syrah and Grenache, rosés also on Cinsault, and whites on Viognier, Grenache Blanc, Marsanne and Roussanne.

france/gros-plant-du-pays-nantais.text: A Loire Valley appellation, mostly in the Loire-Atlantique, for white wine made from Folle Blanche.

france/haut-montravel.text: A Bergerac appellation in South West France. It makes sweet white wine from Sémillon, Sauvignon and Muscadelle, with Ondenc allowed too.

france/hautes-cotes-de-beaune.text: A Burgundy sub-region on top of and behind the Côte de Beaune escarpment, in valleys and slopes. Its wines are labeled Bourgogne Hautes Côtes de Beaune, a named area within the Bourgogne AOC, for red wine based on Pinot Noir, white from Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc, and some rosé. It has no Premier Cru vineyards.

cite.name: Cahier des charges de l'AOC Bourgogne, homologué par l'arrêté du 6 janvier 2026 (BO Agri du 15 janvier 2026)

france/hautes-cotes-de-nuits.text: A Burgundy sub-region on top of and behind the Côte de Nuits escarpment, in valleys and slopes. Its wines are labeled Bourgogne Hautes Côtes de Nuits, a named area within the Bourgogne AOC, for red wine based on Pinot Noir, white from Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc, and some rosé. It has no Premier Cru vineyards.

cite.name: Cahier des charges de l'AOC Bourgogne, homologué par l'arrêté du 6 janvier 2026 (BO Agri du 15 janvier 2026)

france/hermitage.text: A northern Rhône appellation on a hill south of Lyon, making mostly red wine from Syrah. The white, from Marsanne and Roussanne, is around 30% of the wine. Some see the hill as the spiritual home of Syrah.

france/irancy.text: A Burgundy appellation in the Grand Auxerrois, in the Yonne, for red wine made from Pinot Noir across three communes. César and Pinot Gris are allowed in small amounts.

france/julienas.text: A Beaujolais cru for red wine made from Gamay. It sits on the north bank of the Mauvaise valley and is said to take its name from Julius Caesar.

france/jurancon.text: A South West appellation in the Pyrenees foothills, making dry and sweet white wine. Both come from Petit Manseng and Gros Manseng on steep slopes, with tropical aromas such as pineapple and mango in the sweet wines.

france/l-etoile.text: A Jura appellation of four communes, making white wine from Savagnin Blanc and Chardonnay, with Poulsard also allowed. Its types include wine from raisined grapes. Jura is a cool-climate region best known for vin jaune.

france/lalande-de-pomerol.text: A Bordeaux Right Bank appellation for red wine, just north of Pomerol across the Barbanne stream. It is made from Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon and Malbec, and it covers two communes, Lalande-de-Pomerol and Néac.

france/latricieres-chambertin.text: A Grand Cru in Gevrey-Chambertin, in the Côte de Nuits, making only red wine, from Pinot Noir. Chardonnay, Pinot Blanc and Pinot Gris are allowed only as vines mixed into the vineyard, up to 15% of each plot.

france/limoux.text: A Languedoc-Roussillon appellation around Limoux, covering sparkling and still wines. Mauzac, Chardonnay and Chenin Blanc are used for whites, and reds are blended from Merlot, Malbec, Syrah, Grenache, Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon. Limoux claims the world's first sparkling wine, made by monks at Saint-Hilaire and recorded in 1531.

france/loire-valley.text: The wine regions along the Loire river, from Muscadet on the Atlantic coast to Sancerre in the east, with smaller vineyards further upstream in the Massif Central, such as Saint-Pourçain and Côte Roannaise.

france/loupiac.text: A Bordeaux appellation in Entre-Deux-Mers, between the Garonne and Dordogne rivers. Loupiac covers one commune and makes sweet white wine from Sémillon, Sauvignon Blanc, Sauvignon Gris and Muscadelle.

france/madiran.text: A South West France appellation of about 3,200 acres, spread over three départements, for red wine built on Tannat, with Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Fer and Manseng Noir in smaller roles. White Pacherenc du Vic-Bilh comes from the same area.

france/mailly-champagne.text: A cru village in the Montagne de Reims, a Champagne sub-region with chalk-based soils. Mailly-Champagne is one of the area's Grand Cru villages.

france/marsannay.text: A Côte de Nuits appellation, the only village appellation in Burgundy allowed to make rosé. Red wine from Pinot Noir is about 70 percent of production, rosé comes from Pinot Noir and Pinot Gris, and white from Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc. It has no Grand Cru or Premier Cru vineyards.

france/maury.text: A Roussillon appellation for vin doux naturel, sweet wine fortified by adding spirit during fermentation, with the red styles led by Grenache. Since 2011 it also covers dry, still red wine, and in 2010 output was split about evenly between the two.

france/medoc.text: A Left Bank Bordeaux appellation whose zone covers the whole Médoc peninsula, though in practice the name is used mainly in the north, sometimes called Bas-Médoc. It is almost all red, from Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc and others, with a small but growing amount of white.

france/menetou-salon.text: An appellation of ten communes, making white from Sauvignon Blanc and red and rosé from Pinot Noir.

france/montagne-de-reims.text: A Champagne sub-region around Reims Mountain between Reims and Épernay, with nine Grand Cru villages. Its soils are chalk-based and Pinot Noir is the main grape.

france/montagne-saint-emilion.text: A Bordeaux appellation on the Right Bank of the Dordogne, making only red wine, mainly from Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon and Cot.

france/muscadet.text: A Loire Valley AOC for still white wine from the Pays nantais, at the western end of the valley. It is made mainly from Melon, and current rules allow up to 10% Chardonnay.

france/muscat-de-frontignan.text: A Languedoc-Roussillon appellation for vin doux naturel and liqueur wine made from Muscat à Petits Grains, white or red. It comes from the communes of Frontignan and Vic-la-Gardiole in Hérault.

france/muscat-de-mireval.text: A Languedoc-Roussillon appellation in Hérault for white vin doux naturel made from Muscat à Petits Grains. It covers the communes of Mireval and Vic-la-Gardiole.

france/muscat-de-saint-jean-de-minervois.text: A Languedoc-Roussillon appellation for vin doux naturel, a fortified sweet wine, made from white Muscat à Petits Grains. It comes from a single commune, Saint-Jean-de-Minervois, in Hérault.

cite.name: INAO, product sheet AOP Muscat de Saint-Jean-de-Minervois

france/northern-rhone.text: A Rhône Valley area whose appellations include Côte-Rôtie, Hermitage, Cornas, Saint-Joseph, Crozes-Hermitage and Condrieu.

france/nuits-saint-georges.text: A Côte de Nuits village in Burgundy. It has no Grand Cru vineyards.

france/orleans.text: A Loire Valley appellation around the city of Orléans for white, red and rosé wines. Whites are led by Chardonnay, and reds and rosés by Meunier. Pinot Noir and Pinot Gris play smaller roles.

france/pacherenc-du-vic-bilh.text: A South West France appellation for white wine, sweet or dry. Sweet wines are led by Petit Manseng. Dry wines, labeled sec, are led by Petit Manseng, Gros Manseng and Petit Courbu, with Arrufiac, Courbu and Sauvignon in smaller roles.

france/pernand-vergelesses.text: A Côte de Beaune village in Burgundy making red wine from Pinot Noir and white from Chardonnay. It holds the western side of the Corton hill, with vineyards of all three Corton Grand Crus.

france/pessac-leognan.text: The northern part of Graves in Bordeaux, making red and dry white wines, with red over 80% of the wine. It includes Château Haut-Brion, and its classed growths are about a third of its estates.

france/pierry.text: A Champagne cru village whose wines may be labeled premier cru. The Champagne appellation is reserved for sparkling white and rosé wines.

cite.name: Cahier des charges de l’appellation d'origine contrôlée Champagne, homologué par l'arrêté du 31 juillet 2025 (AGRT2518163A) - BO n°32 du 7 août 2025

france/pomerol.text: A Right Bank appellation in Bordeaux, covering the commune of Pomerol and part of Libourne, whose wine is mostly Merlot with Cabernet Franc in support. It became AOC in 1936.

france/pouilly-fuisse.text: A Mâconnais appellation for white wine made only from Chardonnay in Fuissé, Solutré-Pouilly, Vergisson and Chaintré. Its rules now let 22 of its climats be labeled premier cru.

france/pouilly-vinzelles.text: A Mâconnais appellation for white wine made only from Chardonnay, in the commune of Vinzelles. Three of its climats, Les Longeays, Les Pétaux and Les Quarts, may be labeled premier cru. It sits next to Pouilly-Fuissé and Pouilly-Loché.

cite.name: Cahier des charges de l'AOP Pouilly-Vinzelles, homologué par l'arrêté du 18 novembre 2024 (JORF du 20 novembre 2024)

france/premieres-cotes-de-bordeaux.text: A Bordeaux appellation for sweet white wine in Entre-Deux-Mers, across thirty-nine communes including Bassens, Baurech and Bouliac. Its wines are made from Sémillon, Sauvignon, Sauvignon Gris and Muscadelle.

france/puisieulx.text: A cru village in the Montagne de Reims, a Champagne sub-region where soils are chalk-based. It is one of the communes whose champagnes may be labeled grand cru.

cite.name: Cahier des charges de l’appellation d'origine contrôlée Champagne, homologué par l'arrêté du 31 juillet 2025 (AGRT2518163A) - BO n°32 du 7 août 2025

france/puligny-montrachet.text: A Côte de Beaune village in Burgundy making almost only white wine, from Chardonnay. It has four Grand Cru vineyards, with Montrachet the best known, and 17 Premier Crus.

france/quarts-de-chaume.text: A Loire Valley appellation for sweet white wine made only from Chenin, grown in the single commune of Rochefort-sur-Loire. Its label may add grand cru.

france/rhone-valley.text: A wine region of France divided into the Northern Rhône and the Southern Rhône. Its appellations include Cairanne, Vinsobres and Costières de Nîmes.

france/right-bank.text: A Bordeaux area holding appellations such as Saint-Émilion Grand Cru, Pomerol, Fronsac, Castillon Côtes de Bordeaux and Côtes de Bourg.

france/rivesaltes.text: A Languedoc-Roussillon appellation, mostly in Roussillon with a few communes in the Aude, for naturally sweet fortified wine, a style called vin doux naturel.

france/romanee-conti.text: A Grand Cru vineyard in Vosne-Romanée in the Côte de Nuits, making red wine mainly from Pinot Noir. It is a monopole of the Domaine de la Romanée-Conti.

france/rose-d-anjou.text: A Loire Valley rosé appellation whose main grapes are Grolleau and Grolleau Gris. Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Malbec, Gamay and Pineau d'Aunis are allowed in smaller roles.

france/rose-des-riceys.text: A rosé from the three villages of Les Riceys in the Aube, in Champagne, made only from Pinot Noir. It can be aged in tank for early drinking or in wood for longer keeping, and has a distinctive taste the French call goût des Riceys.

france/rosette.text: A Bergerac appellation in South West France for white wine with some sweetness, in the style called moelleux, made from Sauvignon Blanc, Sauvignon Gris, Sémillon and Muscadelle. It covers six communes around Bergerac in Dordogne.

france/saint-chinian.text: A Languedoc-Roussillon appellation for red, rosé and white wines, which must be blends of at least two grapes. Reds can use Syrah, Grenache, Carignan, Mourvèdre and Cinsault, and whites must include Grenache Blanc, with Marsanne, Roussanne and Vermentino as the other main grapes. It has had AOC protection since 1982.

france/saint-emilion.text: A Right Bank Bordeaux appellation for red wine, around the town of Saint-Émilion just east of Libourne, above the Dordogne. Its wines are made mainly from Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon. Its vineyard landscape was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1999.

france/saint-emilion-grand-cru.text: A Bordeaux appellation for red wine, covering eight communes around Saint-Émilion and part of Libourne. Wines are made from Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Malbec and Carmenère.

france/saint-estephe.text: A Left Bank Bordeaux appellation in the Médoc for red wine. The 1855 classification ranks five of its estates as classified growths.

france/saint-georges-saint-emilion.text: A Right Bank Bordeaux appellation for red wine from Saint-Georges, a village and former commune that has been part of Montagne since 1973.

france/sainte-foy-bordeaux.text: A Bordeaux appellation in Entre-Deux-Mers for red and white wine, with whites made dry, medium-sweet or sweet. Reds use Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc and Malbec, and whites Sémillon, Sauvignon Blanc, Sauvignon Gris and Muscadelle.

france/saone-et-loire.text: A French IGP for the Saône-et-Loire département. Across all the département's vineyards, whatever name the wine is sold under, Chardonnay leads with about 57% of vines, followed by Pinot Noir and Gamay.

france/saussignac.text: A Bergerac appellation in South West France making only sweet white wine. It comes from overripe grapes concentrated by noble rot or by drying on the vine, and adding sugar is forbidden.

france/sauternes.text: A Bordeaux appellation within Sauternes & Barsac for sweet white wine from Sémillon, Sauvignon Blanc and Muscadelle affected by noble rot (Botrytis cinerea). Its climate often brings noble rot, though harvests vary widely between vintages.

france/sermiers.text: A Champagne village whose wines may be labeled Premier Cru. Champagne itself is a sparkling wine, white or rosé.

cite.name: Cahier des charges de l’appellation d'origine contrôlée Champagne, homologué par l'arrêté du 31 juillet 2025 (AGRT2518163A) - BO n°32 du 7 août 2025

france/sillery.text: A Grand Cru village in the Montagne de Reims, a Champagne sub-region with chalk-based soils and nine Grand Cru villages.

cite.name: Cahier des charges de l’appellation d'origine contrôlée Champagne, homologué par l'arrêté du 31 juillet 2025 (AGRT2518163A) - BO n°32 du 7 août 2025

france/taissy.text: A Premier Cru village in Champagne, so its wines are made under Champagne rules: quality sparkling wine from Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Meunier and a few rarer allowed grapes.

cite.name: Cahier des charges de l’appellation d'origine contrôlée Champagne, homologué par l'arrêté du 31 juillet 2025 (AGRT2518163A) - BO n°32 du 7 août 2025

france/tavel.text: A southern Rhône appellation that makes only rosé, across the river from Châteauneuf-du-Pape, in the commune of Tavel and part of Roquemaure. Allowed grapes include Grenache, Cinsault, Syrah, Mourvèdre and Clairette.

france/terrasses-du-larzac.text: A Languedoc appellation for red and white wines. The reds are blended mainly from Grenache, Mourvèdre, Syrah and Carignan, with Cinsault and a few other grapes in smaller roles.

france/touraine.text: A broad Loire Valley appellation for white, red and rosé wines, with sparkling white and rosé also allowed. Most of it is white, and the reds range from light, fruity Gamay to firmer Cabernet Franc wines and blends. It covers the same ground as many smaller local appellations.

france/tours-sur-marne.text: A Grand Cru village inside Champagne. Allowed grapes include Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Meunier, plus rarer ones such as Petit Meslier and Arbane.

cite.name: Cahier des charges de l’appellation d'origine contrôlée Champagne, homologué par l'arrêté du 31 juillet 2025 (AGRT2518163A) - BO n°32 du 7 août 2025

france/trepail.text: One of Champagne's Premier Cru villages, making sparkling wine under the Champagne rules. Those allow Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Meunier, along with rarer grapes such as Pinot Blanc, Pinot Gris, Petit Meslier and Arbane.

cite.name: Cahier des charges de l’appellation d'origine contrôlée Champagne, homologué par l'arrêté du 31 juillet 2025 (AGRT2518163A) - BO n°32 du 7 août 2025

france/trois-puits.text: A Premier Cru village in Champagne, so its wines are made under Champagne rules: quality sparkling wine from Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Meunier and a few rarer allowed grapes.

cite.name: Cahier des charges de l’appellation d'origine contrôlée Champagne, homologué par l'arrêté du 31 juillet 2025 (AGRT2518163A) - BO n°32 du 7 août 2025

france/vacqueyras.text: A southern Rhône cru, at the foot of the Dentelles de Montmirail. It is mostly red, led by Grenache with Syrah and Mourvèdre, with some white and rosé.

france/valencay.text: A Touraine appellation in the upper Loire, on the left bank of the Cher. The name is shared with a protected goat's cheese. Sauvignon Blanc is the main white grape, and reds are made from Malbec, Gamay and Pinot Noir.

france/var.text: An IGP covering the whole Var department in Provence. Grenache, Cinsault and Syrah are the most planted grapes across the department's vineyards.

france/ventoux.text: A southeastern Rhône appellation. Reds are made mainly from Grenache, Syrah, Mourvèdre, Cinsault and Carignan, whites from grapes such as Clairette and Roussanne.

france/verzy.text: One of Champagne's cru villages, making sparkling wine under the Champagne rules. Those allow Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Meunier, along with Pinot Blanc, Pinot Gris, Petit Meslier, Arbane and Chardonnay Rose, with the new variety Voltis allowed on up to 5 percent of a grower's vines.

cite.name: Cahier des charges de l’appellation d'origine contrôlée Champagne, homologué par l'arrêté du 31 juillet 2025 (AGRT2518163A) - BO n°32 du 7 août 2025

france/villers-aux-noeuds.text: One of Champagne's cru villages, making sparkling wine under the Champagne rules. Those allow Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Meunier, along with Pinot Blanc, Pinot Gris, Petit Meslier, Arbane and Chardonnay Rose, with the new variety Voltis allowed on up to 5 percent of a grower's vines.

cite.name: Cahier des charges de l’appellation d'origine contrôlée Champagne, homologué par l'arrêté du 31 juillet 2025 (AGRT2518163A) - BO n°32 du 7 août 2025

france/vinsobres.text: A southern Rhône appellation for red wine and, since 2026, white wine. It became its own AOC in 2006 as a Rhône cru after belonging to Côtes-du-Rhône Villages. Some vineyards were once olive groves.

france/vire-clesse.text: A Mâconnais appellation for white wine in Burgundy, in the communes of Clessé, Laizé, Montbellet and Viré. Chardonnay is the main grape. Created in 1999, it has no Premier Cru vineyards.

france/vosne-romanee.text: A Côte de Nuits village in Burgundy, used only for red wine, mainly from Pinot Noir. It has six Grand Cru vineyards, including Romanée-Conti, among Burgundy's most iconic red wines, plus two in neighboring Flagey-Échezeaux.

germany.text: Mainly a white wine country along the Rhine and its tributaries, known above all for Riesling, which makes wines from crisp and dry to sweet and intensely aromatic. Riesling is the top grape at 23% of vines. Red varieties cover just under a third of the vineyard, led by Spätburgunder.

germany/ahr.text: One of Germany's smaller wine regions, in the valley of the Ahr, a tributary of the Rhine. Spätburgunder covers about 63% of the area.

germany/baden.text: Germany's third-largest wine region, in the southwest. Cooperatives and their members farm about two thirds of its vineyard area. Spätburgunder leads at 36% of the vines, then Müller-Thurgau, Grauburgunder and Weissburgunder.

germany/franken.text: A wine region in northern Bavaria. Silvaner and Müller-Thurgau lead the plantings, each with about a quarter of the vines, and Bacchus is third.

germany/mosel.text: A region along the Mosel, Saar and Ruwer rivers known for steep vineyard slopes above the water, including Bremmer Calmont, often called Europe's steepest vineyard. Riesling is its main grape, at 61% of vines. Northerly Rieslings are often light, lower in alcohol, crisp and high in acidity.

germany/nahe.text: A Rhineland-Palatinate region along the River Nahe. Its soils are very varied, from volcanic rock to slate, sandstone and loess.

germany/pfalz.text: Germany's second-largest wine region, with about 58,560 acres under vine in 2022. Known as Rheinpfalz before 1993. Riesling leads the plantings at 24%, followed by the red Dornfelder at 14%, with Müller-Thurgau and Spätburgunder behind.

germany/rheinhessen.text: Germany's largest wine region, on the left bank of the Rhine between Worms and Bingen. It makes mostly white wine, led by Riesling and Müller-Thurgau, and is the main source of Liebfraumilch.

germany/wurzburger-stein-berg.text: A Franken site in the commune of Würzburg. Its rules allow only still white wine, from Grüner Silvaner, Riesling and Weissburgunder.

cite.name: Produktspezifikation g.U. Würzburger Stein-Berg (BLE)

greece/candia.text: A Cretan PDO for dry white and red wine. Whites are at least 85% Vilana, with Assyrtiko, Athiri, Thrapsathiri and Vidiano allowed, and reds are made from Kotsifali and Mandilaria.

greece/dafnes.text: A Cretan PDO for dry red wine from Liatiko, with up to 20% Mandilaria allowed. It also allows sweet red liqueur wine and wine from raisined grapes, made from Liatiko.

cite.name: PDO-GR-A1390 Dafnes, amendment application and single document, Ares(2017)3997736 (eAmbrosia)

greece/limnos.text: A PDO on the North Aegean island of Limnos for white wine from Moschato Alexandreias and red wine from Limnio. It also allows sweet red liqueur wine and wine from raisined grapes, mostly from Limnio.

greece/malvasia.text: A Cretan PDO for sweet white wine, made as liqueur wine or wine from raisined grapes. It is at least 85% Assyrtiko, Athiri, Thrapsathiri and Liatiko, with up to 15% Malvasia di Candia Aromatica and Moschato Aspro.

greece/malvasia-candia.text: A Cretan PDO for sweet white wine, made as liqueur wine or wine from raisined grapes. It is at least 85% Assyrtiko, Athiri, Vidiano, Thrapsathiri and Liatiko, with up to 15% Malvasia di Candia Aromatica and Moschato Aspro.

greece/mantinia.text: A Peloponnese PDO for dry white wine and quality sparkling wine, made from at least 85% Moschofilero with Asproudes for the rest.

greece/santorini.text: A Cycladic island in the Aegean Islands group whose wines, above all Vinsanto, were counted among the great wines of the Aegean under Venetian rule. The PDO centers on white grapes such as Assyrtiko, Athiri and Aidani Aspro, and covers dry wine, fortified wine and Vinsanto, made from sun-dried grapes.

italy/aglianico-del-vulture-superiore.text: A Basilicata DOCG for red wine made only from Aglianico, which the rules also name Aglianico del Vulture.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione DOCG Aglianico del Vulture Superiore, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/albugnano.text: A Piedmont DOC for red and rosé wine led by Nebbiolo, at least 85%, with Freisa, Barbera and Bonarda allowed up to 15%. It comes from four communes including Albugnano and Pino d'Asti.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione DOC Albugnano, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/aleatico-di-puglia.text: A Puglia DOC for sweet red wine from Aleatico, at least 85%, with Negroamaro, Malvasia Nera and Primitivo allowed for the rest. It is made as a naturally sweet wine and as a fortified liqueur wine.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione DOC Aleatico di Puglia, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/alezio.text: A Puglia DOC in the province of Lecce for red and rosé wine from Negroamaro, with Malvasia Nera di Lecce, Montepulciano and Sangiovese allowed up to 20%.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione DOC Alezio, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/alto-adige.text: South Tyrol, an autonomous province in northeast Italy. It was part of the Austro-Hungarian County of Tyrol until 1918, and its wine shows strong Austrian influence.

italy/ansonica-costa-dell-argentario.text: A dry white wine from Ansonica, also called Inzolia, on the far southern coast of Tuscany and the island of Giglio. The zone is very sunny, with little rain and dry summers.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione DOC Ansonica Costa dell'Argentario, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/asolo-prosecco.text: A DOCG in Treviso province for Prosecco from Glera, with up to 15% Verdiso, Bianchetta Trevigiana, Perera and Glera Lunga. It is made as spumante, labeled Superiore, as frizzante and as still wine.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione DOCG Asolo Prosecco o Asolo, as amended DM 09.09.2024

italy/asti.text: A DOCG for white wines from Moscato Bianco, grown in the hills of the Asti, Cuneo and Alessandria provinces of Piedmont. Asti spumante is fully sparkling and may be dry or sweet, while Moscato d'Asti is sweet, gently fizzy and low in alcohol. More than 90 million bottles were made in 2024.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOCG Asti (Regione Piemonte consolidated text, 2025)

italy/barbera-d-alba.text: A Piedmont DOC for red wine from Barbera, with up to 15% Nebbiolo allowed. Its zone covers Alba and many communes around it in Cuneo province, including Barbaresco, Neive and part of La Morra.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Barbera d'Alba, consolidated by DM 6 Aug 2021

italy/bardolino.text: A DOC on the moraine hills east of Lake Garda in Verona province, for red wine and the rosé Chiaretto, which may also be sparkling. Corvina leads the blend, with Rondinella, and Molinara is now optional.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Bardolino, as amended by DM 2 Apr 2021

italy/barletta.text: A DOC in the Barletta-Andria-Trani province of Apulia. Its reds and rosés are made mainly from Uva di Troia, and its whites mainly from Malvasia Bianca.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Barletta, as amended 2014

italy/bianchello-del-metauro.text: Bianchello del Metauro makes white wine, still and sparkling, from at least 95% Biancame, with a little Malvasia Bianca Lunga allowed.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Bianchello del Metauro, as amended 2014

italy/brachetto-d-acqui.text: A DOCG for wine from the Brachetto grape, made in the hills around Acqui Terme, across the provinces of Asti and Alessandria. The wine is aromatic and ruby to rosé in color. It can be still, lightly sparkling or fully sparkling, from dry to sweet, and there is also a sweet passito.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOCG Brachetto d'Acqui o Acqui, as amended by DM 7 Aug 2019

italy/brindisi.text: A DOC in the province of Brindisi, in Apulia, for red, rosé and white wine, some of it sparkling.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Brindisi, as amended by DM 7 Mar 2014

italy/brunello-di-montalcino.text: A red DOCG made only from Sangiovese around Montalcino, in the province of Siena, Tuscany. Brunello was once taken for a separate grape, until a Siena ampelographic commission working from 1877 to 1883 found it was Sangiovese.

italy/campania.text: An IGT for the whole of Campania, whose area includes Taurasi, Fiano di Avellino, Greco di Tufo and Vesuvio. Vineyards are planted above all to Aglianico (33%) and Falanghina Flegrea (19%), then Barbera (7%) and Greco (6%).

italy/cartizze.text: A place inside the Conegliano Valdobbiadene Prosecco Superiore DOCG in Veneto, where the name Superiore di Cartizze is reserved for sparkling wine made from Glera. Verdiso, Perera and Bianchetta Trevigiana are also allowed there.

cite.name: Production regulations for Conegliano Valdobbiadene - Prosecco DOCG, English text, December 2018

italy/castel-del-monte-nero-di-troia-ris.text: A Puglia denomination for riserva wine only, from communes around Andria, Trani and Bitonto.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione DOCG Castel del Monte Nero di Troia Riserva, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/casteller.text: A Trentino denomination spread over dozens of communes, from Riva del Garda to Trento and Rovereto. Its rules require at least 50% Merlot, with only Lagrein, Teroldego, Lambrusco A Foglia Frastagliata and two Schiava types allowed for the rest.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione DOC Casteller, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/castelli-romani.text: A Lazio denomination covering communes including Frascati, Marino, Velletri and Nemi, plus part of Rome. Its rules allow still and semi-sparkling wine.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione DOC Castelli Romani, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/cesanese-del-piglio.text: A Lazio DOCG centered on Piglio, with Anagni, Paliano and two other communes. Its rules require at least 90% Cesanese d'Affile and/or Cesanese Comune, both red grapes.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOCG Cesanese del Piglio o Piglio, as amended by DM 07.03.2014

italy/cesanese-di-affile.text: A Lazio denomination limited to the communes of Affile, Arcinazzo Romano and Roiate. Its rules cover only still red wine, from at least 90% Cesanese d'Affile.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Cesanese di Affile o Affile, as amended by DM 07.03.2014

italy/cesanese-di-olevano-romano.text: A Lazio denomination limited to the communes of Genazzano and Olevano Romano. Its rules allow still and semi-sparkling wine, from at least 85% of the red Cesanese Comune and Cesanese d'Affile.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Cesanese di Olevano Romano o Olevano Romano, as amended by DM 07.03.2014

italy/chianti.text: A Tuscan red wine made principally from Sangiovese. It was once tied to a straw-covered flask, the fiasco. Chianti was first given legal boundaries in 1716, for the hills now covered by the separate Chianti Classico DOCG.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOCG Chianti Classico, as amended by DM 22.06.2023

italy/circeo.text: A Lazio denomination limited to four communes: Latina, Sabaudia, San Felice Circeo and Terracina. Its rules allow still, semi-sparkling and sparkling wine.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Circeo, as amended by DM 07.03.2014

italy/colli-dell-etruria-centrale.text: A Tuscan denomination spread over many communes, including Florence, Arezzo and Montalcino.

italy/colli-della-sabina.text: A Lazio denomination from communes such as Fara in Sabina, Poggio Mirteto and Palombara Sabina. Its rules cover white and red wine.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Colli della Sabina, as amended by DM 07.03.2014

italy/colli-perugini.text: An Umbrian denomination covering parts of seven communes around Perugia, Deruta and Marsciano. Its rules allow still and sparkling wine.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Colli Perugini, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/colline-joniche-tarantine.text: A Puglia denomination from communes such as Castellaneta, Ginosa and Grottaglie. Its rules allow still, sparkling and liqueur wine.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Colline Joniche Tarantine, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/colline-teramane-montepulciano-dab.text: An Abruzzo DOCG in the province of Teramo for red wine from at least 90% Montepulciano, with up to 10% Sangiovese allowed.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOCG Colline Teramane Montepulciano d'Abruzzo, as amended by Reg. (UE) 2023/2171

italy/conegliano-valdobbiadene-prosecco-.text: A Veneto DOCG in the hills of Treviso province, between Vittorio Veneto and Valdobbiadene. Its wine is made from Glera, with up to 15% Verdiso, Bianchetta Trevigiana, Perera and Glera Lunga allowed, in sparkling, semi-sparkling and still styles. Cartizze lies inside.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOCG Conegliano Valdobbiadene - Prosecco, as amended under Reg. (UE) 2019/33

italy/contea-di-sclafani.text: A Sicilian DOC for white and red wine. The white is at least 95% Catarratto, and the red is made from Nero d'Avola, Perricone or both in any proportion.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Contea di Sclafani o Valledolmo-Contea di Sclafani, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/copertino.text: A Puglia denomination from six communes around Copertino and Galatina. Its wine is made from Negroamaro, with Malvasia Nera di Brindisi, Malvasia Nera di Lecce, Montepulciano and Sangiovese allowed up to 30% together.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Copertino, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/cori.text: A Lazio denomination covering all of Cori and part of Cisterna di Latina.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Cori, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/corti-benedettine-del-padovano.text: A Veneto denomination. Its rules allow still wines, a semi-sparkling Chardonnay, and sparkling Chardonnay and Moscato.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Corti Benedettine del Padovano, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/delle-venezie.text: A DOC covering the province of Trento, Friuli-Venezia Giulia and Veneto. Its rules cover Pinot Grigio, still, semi-sparkling or sparkling and also in a rosé or ramato version, plus a white blend.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC delle Venezie, as amended DM 15.07.2021

italy/dolcetto-d-alba.text: A Piedmont red wine made from Dolcetto alone, from communes around Alba, Barolo and Barbaresco among them. Its zone lies almost wholly in the province of Cuneo, with one commune in Asti province.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Dolcetto d'Alba, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/elba.text: A DOC for wine from the island of Elba, off Tuscany. Its rules cover red, rosé, white and sparkling wines, plus sweet passito wines and Vin Santo.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Elba, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/etna.text: A Sicilian DOC on Mount Etna, the highest active volcano in Europe, where vines have long played a major role. Its reds and rosés are made mostly from Nerello Mascalese, and its still whites from Carricante.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Etna, as amended by DM 19 Jan 2022 (rectified 14 Mar 2022)

italy/falerno-del-massico.text: A DOC in Caserta province, in Campania, from five communes including Carinola and Sessa Aurunca. It makes a white from Falanghina, a red led by Aglianico with Piedirosso, and a Primitivo.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Falerno del Massico, as amended by DM 7 Mar 2014

italy/faro.text: A Sicilian red DOC limited to the commune of Messina. It is made mainly from Nerello Mascalese, Nerello Cappuccio and Nocera, with up to 15% Calabrese, Gaglioppo or Sangiovese.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Faro, as amended by DM 7 Mar 2014

italy/fiano-di-avellino.text: A Campania white from 26 communes around Avellino, made from at least 85% Fiano, with Greco, Coda di Volpe Bianca and Trebbiano Toscano allowed in the rest.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOCG Fiano di Avellino, as amended by DM 13 Oct 2020

italy/frascati.text: A white wine from the hills around Frascati, southeast of Rome, in Lazio, made still and sparkling. It is at least 70% Malvasia Bianca di Candia and Malvasia del Lazio, with Bellone, Bombino Bianco, Greco Bianco and Trebbiano in smaller roles.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Frascati, as amended by DM 7 Mar 2014

italy/freisa-d-asti.text: A Piedmont wine made from at least 90% Freisa, from the hills of Asti province. Its rules allow still, semi-sparkling and sparkling wine.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Freisa d'Asti, as amended by DM 3 Nov 2021

italy/friuli-colli-orientali.text: A Friuli-Venezia Giulia DOC in Udine province, with Cialla among its subzones. Ramandolo and Rosazzo, once part of it, are now DOCGs of their own.

italy/gabiano.text: A Piedmont DOC for red wine, limited to the hillside vineyards of Gabiano and Moncestino in Alessandria province. It is 90 to 95% Barbera, with Freisa, Grignolino, Nebbiolo or Dolcetto making up the rest.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Gabiano, consolidated text published by Regione Piemonte, 2025

italy/gambellara.text: A Veneto white wine DOC from all or part of four communes, including Gambellara. Its rules allow still wine, quality sparkling wine and Vin Santo from at least 80% Garganega, with Chardonnay, Pinot Bianco and Trebbiano di Soave allowed. Garganega is also among the main grapes of Veneto.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Gambellara, as amended by DM 29 Dec 2017

italy/ghemme.text: A red DOCG in the hills of Novara province, in Piedmont, from parts of Ghemme and Romagnano Sesia. It is made mainly from Nebbiolo, locally called Spanna, with Uva Rara and Vespolina allowed. It must age at least 34 months, 18 of them in wood.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOCG Ghemme, consolidated text 2025, Regione Piemonte

italy/gioia-del-colle.text: A Puglia DOC in Bari province for red, rosé and white wine. Reds and rosés are 50 to 60% Primitivo, blended with Montepulciano, Sangiovese, Negroamaro and Malvasia Nera, and the white is mainly Trebbiano Toscano. Its rules also cover a varietal Primitivo and a sweet Aleatico.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Gioia del Colle, as amended 2014

italy/giro-di-cagliari.text: A Sardinian DOC for wine and liqueur wine made from the Girò grape alone, ranging from dry to sweet.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Girò di Cagliari, as amended 2014

italy/grance-senesi.text: A DOC in Siena province covering Asciano, Monteroni d'Arbia, Murlo, Rapolano Terme and part of Sovicille.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Grance Senesi, as amended 2014

italy/grignolino-del-monferrato-casalese.text: A Piedmont DOC for wine made from at least 95% Grignolino, with Freisa and Barbera allowed for the rest. Its rules also cover a quality sparkling rosé.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Grignolino del Monferrato Casalese, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2024/2155

italy/lacrima-di-morro.text: A red DOC in the province of Ancona, in Marche, made from the rare local Lacrima grape. It was created in 1985.

italy/lambrusco-di-sorbara.text: An Emilia-Romagna DOC for sparkling and semi-sparkling red and rosé wine, with a white sparkling version too. Its vineyards must be at least 60% Lambrusco di Sorbara. Lambrusco Salamino and other Lambrusco grapes may make up the rest, within set limits.

cite.name: DM 5 November 2024, ordinary amendments to the disciplinare of the DOC Lambrusco di Sorbara, GU n. 277 of 26 Nov 2024

italy/lambrusco-mantovano.text: A Lombardy DOC in the province of Mantua for semi-sparkling red and rosé wine. It is made mainly from Lambrusco Viadanese, Maestri, Marani and Salamino, with up to 15% Lambrusco di Sorbara, Grasparossa, Ancellotta and Fortana.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Lambrusco Mantovano, as amended by DM 7 Mar 2014

italy/langhe.text: A DOC in the province of Cuneo, Piedmont, named for the hills south and east of the Tanaro river, known for their wines, cheeses and the white truffles of Alba. Its zone also takes in Roero communes north of the river, such as Canale and Montà.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Langhe, as amended by DM 7 Mar 2014

italy/lazio.text: An IGT covering the whole Lazio region, home to DOCs and DOCGs such as Roma, Frascati, Marino, Cesanese del Piglio and Est! Est!! Est!!! di Montefiascone, and to part of the Orvieto DOC. Malvasia Bianca di Candia (26%) and Trebbiano Toscano (23%) are the most planted grapes.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Orvieto

italy/lessona.text: A Piedmont DOC for red wine from the commune of Lessona, made from at least 85% Nebbiolo, with Vespolina and Uva Rara allowed.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Lessona, as amended by DM 7 Mar 2014

italy/lison.text: A dry white DOCG on the plain between the Tagliamento and Livenza rivers, a few miles from the sea. Its zone spans two regions, Veneto and Friuli-Venezia Giulia.

italy/lison-pramaggiore.text: A DOC across Veneto and Friuli Venezia Giulia, in the provinces of Venice, Treviso and Pordenone.

italy/malvasia-di-casorzo-d-asti.text: A Piedmont DOC for sweet red and rosé wine from at least 90% Malvasia di Casorzo, with Freisa, Grignolino and Barbera allowed up to 10%. It is made still or lightly fizzy, as spumante and as passito. The zone covers Casorzo, Grana and Grazzano Badoglio in Asti province and Altavilla Monferrato, Olivola, Ottiglio and Vignale Monferrato in Alessandria province.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Casorzo o Malvasia di Casorzo o Malvasia di Casorzo d'Asti, as amended DM 18.12.2014 and 2019

italy/marsala.text: A Sicilian DOC for fortified wine, dry or sweet, and gold, amber or ruby in color. The zone covers the province of Trapani around the city of Marsala, except Pantelleria, Favignana and Alcamo. Unfortified wine from the area does not qualify.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Marsala, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/matino.text: A Puglia DOC in the province of Lecce for red and rosé wine from Negroamaro, with Malvasia Nera and Sangiovese allowed up to 30% together. Its zone covers Matino and parts of nearby communes such as Gallipoli and Casarano.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Matino, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/monferrato.text: A Piedmont DOC named for the historical region of Monferrato, with a zone across much of the Asti and Alessandria provinces. It covers red, white and Chiaretto rosé wines, plus varietal Dolcetto, Freisa, Nebbiolo and Casalese Cortese.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Monferrato, as amended DM 07.06.2019

italy/monforte-d-alba.text: A commune in the Barolo zone in Piedmont. Barolo is a red DOCG wine made only from Nebbiolo, often described as one of Italy's greatest wines, and part of Monforte d'Alba lies within its zone.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOCG Barolo, as amended DM 17.04.2015

italy/montecarlo.text: A DOC in northern Tuscany, around the town of Montecarlo near Lucca and Pisa. Its white blends 30 to 60% Trebbiano Toscano with at least three of Sémillon, Pinot Grigio, Pinot Bianco, Vermentino, Sauvignon and Roussanne.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Montecarlo, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/morellino-di-scansano.text: A red DOCG from the hills around Scansano in the Maremma, coastal Tuscany. It is made mainly from Sangiovese, which is called Morellino locally.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione DOCG Morellino di Scansano, as amended DM 02.03.2021

italy/moscadello-di-montalcino.text: A sweet white wine from the Tuscan village of Montalcino, made mainly from Moscato Bianco. It comes still, including a late-harvest (vendemmia tardiva) version, or semi-sparkling.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione DOC Moscadello di Montalcino, as amended DM 16.10.2020

italy/moscato-d-asti.text: A sweet, low alcohol, lightly sparkling (frizzante) white wine made from Moscato Bianco under the Asti DOCG in Piedmont, across parts of the provinces of Asti, Cuneo and Alessandria. Asti is a related wine from the same grape and area.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione DOCG Asti, as amended DM 26.08.2024

italy/moscato-di-sardegna.text: A Sardinian DOC with four styles: still, sparkling (spumante), passito from raisined grapes and wine from overripe grapes. Its wine is named for the Moscato grape.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione DOC Moscato di Sardegna, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/moscato-di-trani.text: A Puglia DOC for wine and liqueur wine made mainly from Moscato Bianco, from communes such as Andria, Barletta and Bisceglie.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione DOC Moscato di Trani, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/nardo.text: A Puglia DOC for red and rosé wine made mainly from Negroamaro, with Malvasia Nera di Brindisi, Malvasia Nera di Lecce and Montepulciano allowed, from the communes of Nardò and Porto Cesareo.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione DOC Nardò, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/nasco-di-cagliari.text: A Sardinian DOC for wine and liqueur wine made only from the Nasco grape, in the south and center-west of the island.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione DOC Nasco di Cagliari, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/negroamaro-di-terra-d-otranto.text: A DOC across the provinces of Brindisi, Lecce and Taranto, in Puglia, for red and rosé wine, with the rosé also made semi-sparkling and sparkling. Its wine is named for the Negroamaro grape.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione DOC Negroamaro di Terra d'Otranto, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/neive.text: A Barbaresco commune in Piedmont. Barbaresco is a Nebbiolo wine from the Langhe, east of Alba, and its zone takes in all of Neive, Barbaresco and Treiso and part of Alba. The wine is often compared with Barolo.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOCG Barbaresco, as amended DM 17.04.2015

italy/novello.text: A commune in the Barolo zone in Piedmont. Barolo is a red DOCG wine made from Nebbiolo, often described as one of Italy's greatest wines, and its zone takes in part of Novello.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOCG Barolo, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/orta-nova.text: A Puglia DOC in the province of Foggia for red and rosé wine based on Sangiovese. Uva di Troia, Montepulciano, Lambrusco Maestri and Trebbiano Toscano may make up to 40%, with Lambrusco Maestri and Trebbiano Toscano each capped at 10%.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Orta Nova, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/ostuni.text: A Puglia DOC for a white based on Impigno and Francavidda and a light red from Ottavianello, the local name for Cinsault. The zone covers Ostuni, Carovigno and nearby communes.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Ostuni, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/prosecco-doc.text: A DOC across nine provinces in Veneto and Friuli-Venezia Giulia, made from Glera with up to 15% other grapes such as Chardonnay or Pinot Grigio. It is almost always sparkling or semi-sparkling, though still wine is allowed. The sparkling wine can also be made as a rosé, with 10 to 15% Pinot Nero.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Prosecco, as amended DM 19.06.2023

italy/recioto-della-valpolicella.text: A sweet red DOCG passito from Valpolicella in Veneto. The grapes are dried to concentrate their sugars. The name is usually traced to the local word for ear, used for the wings of the bunch.

italy/recioto-di-gambellara.text: A Veneto DOCG for white Recioto made only from Garganega grapes that are dried after harvest. The Classico is medium-sweet or sweet, and there is also a sparkling version. Its communes are Gambellara, Montebello Vicentino, Montorso Vicentino and Zermeghedo.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOCG Recioto di Gambellara, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/riviera-del-brenta.text: A Veneto appellation for still, semi-sparkling and sparkling wine. It covers communes around Padua, Dolo and Mira.

italy/rosazzo.text: A white DOCG from Udine province in Friuli-Venezia Giulia. It is at least 50% Friulano, with 20 to 30% Sauvignon, 20 to 30% Pinot Bianco or Chardonnay and up to 10% Ribolla Gialla. The zone covers parts of Corno di Rosazzo, Manzano and San Giovanni al Natisone.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOCG Rosazzo, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/rosso-di-cerignola.text: A red wine from Puglia, made in Cerignola, Stornara and Stornarella. It is at least 55% Uva di Troia with 15 to 30% Negroamaro, and up to 15% in all of Sangiovese, Barbera, Montepulciano, Malbec or Trebbiano Toscano.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Rosso di Cerignola, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/rosso-piceno.text: A Marche DOC for red wine. Its zone runs from the border of Pesaro province south to Porto d'Ascoli, leaving out the Rosso Conero zone.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Rosso Piceno o Piceno, as amended DM 01.02.2024

italy/rubino-di-cantavenna.text: A Piedmont appellation for red wine from Gabiano, Moncestino, Villamiroglio and part of Camino. It is made from only three grapes, mainly Barbera with some Freisa and Grignolino.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Rubino di Cantavenna, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/salice-salentino.text: A Puglia DOC around the town of Salice Salentino. Its red and rosé are made mainly from Negroamaro, while the white is based on Chardonnay and Aleatico makes sweet and fortified wines.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Salice Salentino, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/san-torpe.text: A Tuscan DOC in the province of Pisa, reaching into Livorno province at Collesalvetti. Its rules allow still white and rosé wine and Vin Santo.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC San Torpè, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/sannio.text: A Campania DOC covering the whole province of Benevento, for still, semi-sparkling and sparkling wine.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Sannio, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/sant-antimo.text: A Tuscan DOC covering part of the commune of Montalcino, in Siena province.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Sant'Antimo, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/sardegna-semidano.text: A Sardinia DOC for white wine from at least 85% Semidano, made still, sparkling or passito. Its zone is the whole of Sardinia, with a subzone, Mogoro.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Sardegna Semidano, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/taurasi.text: A red wine from Avellino province in Campania, based principally on Aglianico and grown on hillside vineyards. It became a DOC in 1970 and a DOCG in 1993.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOCG Taurasi, as amended DM 14.12.2018

italy/teroldego-rotaliano.text: A Trentino red or rosé made only from Teroldego, from the Campo Rotaliano in Mezzocorona, Mezzolombardo and part of San Michele all'Adige.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Teroldego Rotaliano, as amended DM 14.01.2020

italy/terra-d-otranto.text: A Puglia appellation covering the whole of the provinces of Brindisi, Lecce and Taranto, for still, semi-sparkling and sparkling wine.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Terra d'Otranto, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/terre-alfieri.text: A Piedmont appellation covering San Damiano, San Martino Alfieri and five other communes in Asti province, plus parts of Govone, Priocca, Magliano Alfieri and Castellinaldo in Cuneo province.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOCG Terre Alfieri, DM 09.10.2020
