italy/terre-di-offida.text: A white wine from the Marche, from Ascoli Piceno and Fermo provinces. It is made as quality sparkling wine and from dried grapes as passito and vino santo.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Terre di Offida, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/trebbiano-d-abruzzo.text: A white wine from Abruzzo, made across many communes in all four of its provinces. It must be at least 85% Trebbiano Abruzzese and/or Trebbiano Toscano.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Trebbiano d'Abruzzo, as amended DM 22.12.2014

italy/treiso.text: A Barbaresco commune in Piedmont. Barbaresco is a Nebbiolo wine from the Langhe, east of Alba, and Treiso is one of three communes wholly inside the zone, with Barbaresco and Neive; part of Alba is also included. The wine is often compared with Barolo.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOCG Barbaresco, as amended DM 17.04.2015

italy/trentino.text: A DOC in the southern part of the Trentino-Alto Adige region. It allows still, liqueur and sweet wines. The province grows mostly Pinot Grigio and Chardonnay.

italy/trento-doc.text: A DOC for white and rosé sparkling wine made by bottle fermentation in the province of Trento, from Chardonnay, Pinot Bianco, Pinot Nero and Meunier. Recognized in 1993, it was the first Italian denomination reserved only for traditional method sparkling wine.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Trento, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/valdadige.text: A DOC along the Adige across the provinces of Bolzano, Trento and Verona, for still and semi-sparkling wine.

italy/valdadige-terradeiforti.text: A DOC on the Adige between Trentino and Veneto, limited to the communes of Avio, Brentino Belluno, Dolcè and Rivoli Veronese. Its rules allow still wine.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Valdadige Terradeiforti o Terradeiforti, as amended DM 07.03.2014

italy/valpolicella-ripasso.text: A Veneto red DOC made only in Valpolicella, mainly from Corvina and/or Corvinone with Rondinella. The wine is refermented on the pressed skins left after making Amarone or Recioto della Valpolicella.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Valpolicella Ripasso, as amended DM 03.08.2023

italy/verona.text: An IGT for the Verona area of the Veneto region of Italy.

italy/vesuvio.text: A Campania appellation around Ercolano, Torre del Greco and Boscotrecase, for still, sparkling and liqueur wine. Its whites are led by Caprettone and Coda di Volpe and its reds by Piedirosso. Its white, red and rosé blends may be labeled Lacryma Christi.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Vesuvio, as amended by Reg. UE 2025/1903

italy/vigneti-della-serenissima.text: A Veneto quality sparkling wine made only from Chardonnay, Pinot Bianco and Pinot Nero. It covers hill and mountain vineyards in the provinces of Verona, Vicenza, Padova, Treviso and Belluno, including around Bardolino, Asolo and Bassano del Grappa.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOC Vigneti della Serenissima o Serenissima, as amended by DM 7 Mar 2014

italy/vigneti-delle-dolomiti.text: An IGT covering the whole of the provinces of Bolzano and Trento, and the province of Belluno in Veneto.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione dei vini IGT Vigneti delle Dolomiti, as annexed to the Provincia autonoma di Trento amendment file, July 2026

italy/vino-nobile-di-montepulciano.text: A red DOCG from vineyards around the town of Montepulciano in Tuscany. It is aged at least two years, with at least one year in wood, or three years as riserva.

cite.name: Disciplinare di produzione della DOCG Vino Nobile di Montepulciano, as amended by decree in G.U. n. 29, 5 Feb 2025

new-zealand/bannockburn.text: A geographical indication in Central Otago, on New Zealand's South Island.

portugal/alenquer.text: A valley wine region in Lisboa, where grapes ripen easily into full-bodied reds. Allowed grapes include Touriga Nacional, Castelão, Arinto and Fernão Pires.

portugal/alentejo.text: The DOC for eight subregions of the Alentejo, the large southern region that covers about a third of mainland Portugal and is also noted for cork. Some producers still make wine in clay pots, a practice that goes back to Roman times. Allowed grapes include Alicante Bouschet, Trincadeira, Aragonez and Antão Vaz.

portugal/arruda.text: A Lisboa wine region around the town of Arruda dos Vinhos. Its wines are made from allowed grapes such as Castelão, Touriga Nacional, Aragonez and Alicante Bouschet, with Arinto and Fernão Pires among the whites.

portugal/bairrada.text: A mild, maritime region near the Atlantic, known for deep-colored, tannic reds from Baga. More than half of Portugal's sparkling wine is made here.

portugal/bucelas.text: An area north of Lisbon known for white wine made only from Arinto, Rabo de Ovelha and Sercial. Its whites were once likened in London to Rhine Riesling and called Portuguese hock.

portugal/carcavelos.text: A coastal area between Lisbon and Estoril known for fortified wine, white or red, aged at least two years in wood and marked by an almond note. It was once sought after, but suburban building has since cut it back sharply.

cite.name: Caderno de Especificações DO Carcavelos (PDO-PT-A1462), IVV

portugal/colares.text: A coastal area in Sintra where vines grow in sand behind dunes. Phylloxera never took hold in the sand, so these vines are planted ungrafted. Red Colares from Ramisco is astringent and softens with age, and the whites come from Malvasia.

cite.name: Caderno de Especificações DO Colares (PDO-PT-A1461), IVV

portugal/dao.text: A north central Portuguese region that, along with the Douro, claims to be the original home of Touriga Nacional.

portugal/douro.text: Portugal's river valley best known for Port, though it makes about as much unfortified table wine. Allowed grapes include Rabigato and Touriga Nacional.

portugal/lisboa.text: One of Portugal's largest wine producers by volume, a regional wine area covering the Atlantic strip north of the Tagus estuary, from Lisbon up to the Beira region. Caladoc, Castelão, Fernão Pires and Syrah are the most planted grapes.

cite.name: Caderno de Especificações IG Lisboa, IVV

portugal/minho.text: A regional wine area covering the same ground as the Vinho Verde DOC, differing mainly in allowing international grapes the DOC excludes. Loureiro leads plantings at 30 percent, followed by Arinto and Alvarinho at 16 percent each, with Vinhão, Azal and Trajadura also grown.

cite.name: Caderno de Especificações IG Minho, IVV

portugal/obidos.text: A Lisboa wine region around the town of Óbidos, making red, white and rosé wines as well as sparkling wine. Allowed grapes include Touriga Nacional, Arinto and Fernão Pires.

cite.name: Caderno de Especificações DO Óbidos (PDO-PT-A1469), IVV

portugal/palmela.text: A Setúbal Peninsula DOC on mostly light, sandy soils. Its reds must be at least two-thirds Castelão and its whites are mainly Fernão Pires. It also allows rosé, semi-sparkling, sparkling and liqueur wines.

cite.name: Caderno de Especificações DO Palmela, IVV

portugal/setubal.text: A liqueur wine area known for fortified Muscat wines called Moscatel de Setúbal, with a rarer red-skinned version sold as Moscatel Roxo.

cite.name: Caderno de Especificações DO Setúbal, IVV

portugal/tejo.text: A regional wine area along the Tagus river, which moderates its climate. Fernão Pires is the most planted grape at 37 percent. Until 2009 the regional wine was labeled Ribatejano.

cite.name: Portaria n.º 445/2009, de 27 de Abril (IG Tejo)

portugal/torres-vedras.text: A DOC in the Lisboa region, centered on the town of Torres Vedras. Allowed grapes include Castelão, Touriga Nacional, Aragonez, Arinto and Fernão Pires.

portugal/vinho-verde.text: A northern Portuguese region whose name means green wine, usually explained by the wines' fresh acidity or by the region's lush landscape. The wines can be white, red or rosé, from grapes including Alvarinho, Loureiro, Arinto and Vinhão.

south-africa/walker-bay.text: A district on the Cape South Coast, in the Western Cape, whose wards are Bot River, Hemel-en-Aarde Ridge, Hemel-en-Aarde Valley, Upper Hemel-en-Aarde Valley, Springfontein Rim, Stanford Foothills and Sunday's Glen.

spain.text: Spain has more land planted to vines than any other country, yet it ranks third in wine production. Tempranillo and Airén are the most planted grapes.

cite.name: OIV, State of the World Wine Sector in 2025 (May 2026): Spain the largest vineyard in the world (919 kha) and third largest wine producer

spain/alicante.text: A DO in Alicante province, now divided into several sub-zones. Monastrell suits the dry, limestone soils of the inland Vinalopó, while the coastal Marina Alta has long grown Moscatel. Its traditional wine is Fondillón, made only from Monastrell left to overripen on the vine and aged at least 10 years in oak.

cite.name: Pliego de condiciones DOP Alicante (MAPA, version of 25 Jul 2024)

spain/bullas.text: A Murcia DO whose zone includes Bullas, Caravaca de la Cruz and Moratalla. Monastrell is its main grape.

spain/campo-de-borja.text: Campo de Borja is a transition zone between the Ebro plains and the Iberian mountains, with its highest vineyards on the foothills of Moncayo. Garnacha Tinta, Syrah and Cabernet Sauvignon are among its allowed grapes.

spain/carinena.text: An Aragón DO on the Campo de Cariñena plateau. It dates to 1932, one of the oldest DOs in Spain. Its allowed grapes include Garnacha Tinta, Mazuelo, Tempranillo and Syrah.

spain/cataluna.text: A DO whose zone is a long list of municipalities spread across Catalonia, where many vineyards can also supply other Catalan DOs. Allowed grapes are many, from Macabeo and Xarello to Garnacha and Syrah.

cite.name: Plec de condicions de la DOP Catalunya, 2025

spain/cava.text: A Spanish DO for quality sparkling wine, made only by the traditional method as in Champagne. Macabeo, Parellada and Xarello are the traditional grapes. Other allowed grapes include Chardonnay and the reds Pinot Noir, Garnacha Tinta, Monastrell and Trepat. About 95 percent of cava comes from the Penedès area.

spain/chozas-carrascal.text: A Vino de Pago in the municipality of Requena, in Valencia. Wines are made from Bobal, Tempranillo, Garnacha Tinta, Syrah and Cabernets among reds, and Chardonnay, Macabeo and Sauvignon Blanc among whites.

spain/conca-de-barbera.text: A DO in northern Tarragona province, on the plain of the Francolí and Anguera rivers. Its native Trepat grape has long been used for rosé and is now increasingly made as a red.

spain/costers-del-segre.text: A Catalan DO in Lleida province, split into seven sub-zones: Artesa, Urgell, Les Garrigues, Pallars, Raimat, Segrià and Valls del Riu Corb. The allowed grape list is long and varied, from Tempranillo, Garnacha Tinta and Cabernet Sauvignon to Chardonnay, Macabeo and Riesling.

cite.name: Plec de condicions de la DOP Costers del Segre, 2026

spain/dehesa-penalba.text: A Vino de Pago in the municipality of Villabáñez, Valladolid. Its wines are made from four red grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah and Tempranillo.

spain/dominio-de-valdepusa.text: A Vino de Pago in Malpica de Tajo, Toledo. The category requires every grape to come from vineyards in the pago, with the wine made and bottled by their owners. Allowed grapes include Cabernet Sauvignon, Graciano, Petit Verdot and Syrah.

cite.name: Ley 6/2015, de 12 de mayo, de Denominaciones de Origen e Indicaciones Geográficas Protegidas de ámbito territorial supraautonómico, disposición adicional tercera

spain/emporda.text: A Catalan DO in the northeastern corner of Catalonia, in Girona province. Its vineyards lie in two separate zones: Alt Empordà, from around Figueres north to the French border, and Baix Empordà near the Mediterranean. Garnacha, Macabeo, Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah are among its allowed grapes.

cite.name: Plec de condicions DOP Empordà (Consell Regulador DO Empordà)

spain/la-mancha.text: The La Mancha DO spans 182 municipalities across four provinces. Airén and Tempranillo lead its plantings.

spain/los-balagueses.text: A single-estate Vino de Pago in Requena, Valencia. Allowed grapes include Tempranillo, Merlot, Syrah and Bobal for red, and Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc and Tardana for white.

cite.name: Pliego de condiciones del Vino de Pago Los Balagueses, consolidated version (Generalitat Valenciana)

spain/los-cerrillos.text: A single-estate Vino de Pago in Argamasilla de Alba, Castilla-La Mancha. Its red wines are made from Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah and Petit Verdot.

cite.name: Pliego de condiciones de la DOP Los Cerrillos, as amended 2020 (Junta de Castilla-La Mancha)

spain/manzanilla-de-sanlucar.text: A DO for manzanilla, a dry wine made only from Palomino and aged under flor for at least two years in cellars in Sanlúcar de Barrameda, in Cádiz province. It ranges from pale straw to amber and has a saline taste. It can be sold fortified or unfortified.

cite.name: Pliego de condiciones de la DOP Manzanilla-Sanlúcar de Barrameda, consolidated per Orden de 13 de mayo de 2026 (BOJA 95, 20/05/2026)

spain/mentrida.text: A DO in northern Toledo province, bordering Ávila and Madrid, from the foot of the Sierra de Gredos down to the Tagus and a little beyond it. Its municipalities include Talavera de la Reina and Toledo. Garnacha is the main grape, and Tempranillo and Syrah are also allowed.

cite.name: Pliego de condiciones de la DOP Méntrida, Resolución de 02/11/2022 (DOCM núm. 217, 11/11/2022)

spain/mondejar.text: A DO in the south of Guadalajara province, around the town of Mondéjar. Allowed grapes include Tempranillo, Syrah, Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon for red, and Macabeo, Malvar and Verdejo for white.

spain/monterrei.text: A DO in the southeast corner of Ourense province in Galicia. Its zone takes in all or part of eight municipalities, including Verín. Allowed grapes include Godello, Albariño and Treixadura for white, and Mencía for red.

cite.name: Pliego de condiciones DOP Monterrei, July 2025 (AGACAL, Xunta de Galicia)

spain/navarra.text: A DO across the southern half of Navarre, on the lower Pyrenees slopes running down to the Ebro basin. It was once known mainly for rosados but now also makes quality reds and whites. Tempranillo and Garnacha are the most planted grapes.

spain/penedes.text: A Catalan DO in the Penedès & Cava grouping, framed by the coastal Garraf hills and the higher inland mountains. Since the 2025 harvest, all of its production has been certified organic. Allowed grapes include Xarello, Macabeo and Parellada, plus many red and international varieties.

spain/ribeira-sacra.text: A Galician DO in Lugo and Ourense provinces. Vineyards sit on steep slopes in the Miño and Sil river valleys. The region is known for red wines, and Mencía and Godello are among the allowed grapes.

spain/rueda.text: A Castile and León DO across 74 municipalities in Valladolid, Segovia and Ávila, known mainly for white wines from the Verdejo grape. Sauvignon Blanc, Macabeo and Palomino Fino are also allowed.

spain/sierra-de-salamanca.text: A Castile and León protected designation in Salamanca province, known for red wines from the native Rufete grape. Its wines carry the Vino de Calidad label, a Spanish tier between vino de la tierra and DO. Garnacha and Tempranillo are also allowed, along with Macabeo and Palomino for white.

spain/tarragona.text: A Catalan appellation in two subzones, the Camp de Tarragona and part of the Ribera d'Ebre district. Rules allow wine, sparkling, liqueur and raisined-grape wines, from white Macabeo, Xarello and Parellada and reds such as Garnacha Tinta and Trepat.

spain/terra-alta.text: A Catalan appellation. Rules allow Garnacha Blanca, Garnacha Tinta, Macabeo and Syrah among others. Garnacha Blanca, Garnacha Tinta and Garnacha Peluda are its dominant and oldest grapes.

cite.name: Pliego de condiciones DOP Terra Alta, versió març 2020 (INCAVI)

spain/tierra-del-vino-de-zamora.text: A DO in southeastern Zamora province, with ten villages in neighboring Salamanca province, in Castile and León. Its rules cover wine from red Tempranillo, Garnacha Tinta and Cabernet Sauvignon, and from whites including Doña Blanca, Muscat Blanc, Verdejo and Godello.

wiki.title: Tierra del Vino de Zamora DO

cite.name: Pliego de condiciones de la DOP Tierra del Vino de Zamora, revision AM02 (June 2026)

spain/toro.text: A DO in the southeast of Zamora province, in western Castile and León, that also takes in a few villages in Valladolid province. Its rules allow red Tempranillo and Garnacha Tinta, and white Verdejo, Doña Blanca, Albillo Real and Muscat Blanc.

cite.name: Pliego de condiciones de la DOP Toro (MAPA, January 2025)

spain/uruena.text: A single-estate Vino de Pago of 78 hectares in the municipality of Urueña, Valladolid province, in Castile and León. Its rules allow rosé and red wine from four red grapes: Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Syrah.

cite.name: Pliego de condiciones de la DOP Urueña (MAPA, May 2022)

spain/valdeorras.text: A DO on the banks of the Sil river in the northeast of Ourense province, Galicia. Rules allow white Godello, Albariño, Loureira and Treixadura, and red Mencía, Brancellao and Sousón, as well as sparkling and raisined-grape wines.

spain/valdepenas.text: A DO in the south of Castile-La Mancha, shown here with La Mancha, which almost surrounds it. Its traditional clarete was made by fermenting red Tempranillo and white Airén together, a style the current rules no longer list. Rules allow Tempranillo, Airén and Garnacha Tinta, among others.

cite.name: Orden de 3 de febrero de 1976, Reglamento de la Denominación de Origen Valdepeñas (BOE 24 Feb 1976)

spain/valencia.text: A DO in Valencia province, divided into four subzones: Alto Turia, Valentino, Moscatel de Valencia and Clariano. Across the wider Valencia region, which also takes in Utiel-Requena, Bobal is the most planted grape, at 40 percent.

cite.name: Pliego de condiciones de la DOP Valencia (MAPA, September 2024)

spain/vallegarcia.text: A single-estate Vino de Pago in Castilla-La Mancha. Its red grapes are Syrah, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Petit Verdot, Garnacha Tinta, Mazuelo and Monastrell, with Viognier the only white grape.

cite.name: Amendment PDO-ES-02085-AM01 to the Vallegarcía specification, Official Journal of the EU, C 167, 21 April 2022

spain/valles-de-benavente.text: A Vino de Calidad in northeastern Zamora province, Castile and León, a Spanish tier above Vino de la Tierra and below DO. Its rules allow red Tempranillo, Prieto Picudo, Mencía, Garnacha Tinta and Cabernet Sauvignon, and white Verdejo and Doña Blanca.

cite.name: Pliego de condiciones de la DOP Valles de Benavente (MAPA)

spain/valtiendas.text: A Vino de Calidad of 16 communes in northern Segovia province, whose rules allow wine from red Tempranillo, Garnacha Tinta, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Syrah, with Albillo Mayor the one white grape.

cite.name: Pliego de condiciones de la DOP Valtiendas (MAPA, 2019 revision)

spain/yecla.text: A DO covering the municipality of Yecla, in the northernmost corner of Murcia, surrounded by Jumilla, Almansa and Alicante. Monastrell is its main grape, traditionally made into red wine from old vines.

cite.name: Pliego de condiciones de la DOP Yecla (MAPA, February 2024)

united-kingdom.text: A minor grower of wine, most of it English sparkling wine from southern England. Vineyards are becoming common in counties such as Essex, Sussex and Kent, where the climate is drier and warmer. Chardonnay is the most planted grape, followed by Pinot Noir, Meunier and Bacchus.

cite.name: WineGB 2025 Industry Report (2024 data, Food Standards Agency Wine Team)

united-kingdom/darnibole.text: A UK protected designation of origin in Cornwall for dry still white wine made entirely from Bacchus. Most UK wine is English sparkling wine, from vineyards across southern England.

cite.name: Darnibole Bacchus wine, Protected Designation of Origin product specification (Defra)

united-kingdom/english.text: A protected designation of origin covering England, defined by a long list of English local authorities, for still and quality sparkling wine. Still wine may use a long list of grapes, including Bacchus, Solaris and Rondo. Quality sparkling wine is limited to Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Pinot Noir Précoce, Meunier, Pinot Blanc and Pinot Gris.

cite.name: DEFRA, English Wine Protected Designation of Origin (PDO) specification, December 2011

united-kingdom/welsh.text: A protected designation of origin covering Wales, defined by the Welsh local authorities, for still and quality sparkling wine. Still wine may use a long list of grapes, including Bacchus, Solaris and Rondo. Quality sparkling wine is limited to Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Pinot Noir Précoce, Meunier, Pinot Blanc and Pinot Gris.

cite.name: DEFRA, Welsh Wine Protected Designation of Origin (PDO) specification, December 2011

united-states.text: Wine is made in all fifty states, and the industry rests mainly on European Vitis vinifera, though French-American hybrids are staples on the East Coast. Chardonnay and Cabernet Sauvignon are the most planted grapes at 18% each, then Pinot Noir at 10%. California makes about four fifths of all US wine.

united-states/arroyo-grande-valley.text: A valley AVA in San Luis Obispo County, now within the San Luis Obispo Coast AVA, where Pacific marine air brings frequent fog. Chardonnay and Pinot Noir are the main grapes, grown in the cooler mid-valley, while Zinfandel, Petite Sirah and Rhone varieties are grown on the higher elevations near Lopez Lake.

united-states/arroyo-seco.text: A triangular Monterey County AVA beside Arroyo Seco Creek in the Salinas Valley, near Soledad. The Pacific Ocean and Monterey Bay are its main climate influences, with winds off the bay blowing south up the Salinas Valley to cool it.

united-states/ballard-canyon.text: A canyon of about 7,800 acres at the center of the Santa Ynez Valley in Santa Barbara County, west of the town of Ballard, between Los Olivos and Solvang.

united-states/benmore-valley.text: A mountaintop valley in southwestern Lake County, within the North Coast, much cooler than surrounding areas. Chardonnay was the grape of choice when the AVA was formed, but the valley is not currently planted with vineyards. It is named for a 19th century cattle rustler.

united-states/big-valley-district-lake-c.text: A Clear Lake sub-area on the southern shore of the lake, covering the flatter valley floor north of Kelseyville. Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Viognier and Riesling are the main whites, while Zinfandel, Merlot and Cabernet Franc lead the reds.

united-states/calistoga.text: A Napa Valley sub-area in the northwest of the county, around but not covering the whole town of Calistoga. The town was founded in 1857, and vineyards were established there in 1862.

cite.name: T.D. TTB-83, Establishment of the Calistoga Viticultural Area, 74 FR 64602 (8 Dec 2009)

united-states/candy-mountain.text: A small Columbia Valley AVA on the slopes of Candy Mountain in Benton County, southwest of Richland, inside Yakima Valley.

united-states/capay-valley.text: A California AVA in the Capay Valley of northwestern Yolo County, between the Blue Ridge and the Capay Hills, with Cache Creek running through it.

united-states/cayuga-lake.text: A Finger Lakes sub-area in upstate New York across Cayuga, Seneca and Tompkins counties. Its bedrock is mostly shale, and the lake and steep slopes extend the growing season by keeping cold air from settling on the vines.

united-states/clear-lake.text: A North Coast AVA in Lake County, centered on Clear Lake, the largest natural lake entirely within California. Sub-areas include Big Valley District-Lake County, Kelsey Bench-Lake County and Red Hills Lake County, and most of High Valley lies inside it.

cite.name: 27 CFR part 9, subpart C (American Viticultural Areas), current eCFR

united-states/cole-ranch.text: A tiny Mendocino County AVA in a narrow mountain valley between Boonville and Highway 101, at about 1,400 feet.

united-states/crystal-springs-of-napa-va.text: A small California AVA created in 2024 inside Napa Valley, overlapping none of its neighbors. Calistoga's boundary was moved at the same time so that the whole Crystal Springs Vineyard, part of which had been in Calistoga, lies inside the new AVA.

wiki.title: Crystal Springs of Napa Valley AVA

cite.name: TTB final rule T.D. TTB-197, Establishment of the Crystal Springs of Napa Valley Viticultural Area; Modification of the Calistoga Viticultural Area, 89 FR 83431 (Oct. 16, 2024)

united-states/diablo-grande.text: A California AVA in the western foothills of Stanislaus County. It takes its name from the Diablo Grande resort and residential community that occupies it.

cite.name: ATF final rule, Diablo Grande Viticultural Area (97-104), 63 FR 33850 (June 22, 1998)

united-states/diamond-mountain-district.text: A Napa Valley sub-area in the northwest, higher than most of the valley, so it gets less cool fog. Its very porous soil cools quickly. It rises from the valley floor just southwest of Calistoga.

united-states/dundee-hills.text: A Willamette Valley AVA in Yamhill County near Newberg, with reddish Jory silt, clay and loam soils. The Chehalem Mountains to the north buffer it from Columbia Gorge air, cold in winter and warm in summer. David Lett planted Pinot Noir and Pinot Gris there in 1966.

cite.name: TTB final rule, Establishment of the Dundee Hills Viticultural Area (2002R-218P), 69 FR 69524 (Nov. 30, 2004)

united-states/edna-valley.text: A Central Coast valley in San Luis Obispo County, cooled by frequent summer morning fog and afternoon winds from the ocean, with clay-rich soils. It runs southeast from just beyond the city of San Luis Obispo.

cite.name: ATF final rule T.D. ATF-101, Edna Valley Viticultural Area, 47 FR 20298 (May 12, 1982)

united-states/eola-amity-hills.text: A Willamette Valley AVA of hills west of the Willamette River, from Amity south to Salem, in Polk and Yamhill Counties.

united-states/fair-play.text: A Sierra Foothills AVA in El Dorado County. Zinfandel is the most popular red, and Syrah and Mourvèdre are among its other top varieties.

united-states/finger-lakes.text: An upstate New York AVA south of Lake Ontario. It contains the Cayuga Lake and Seneca Lake AVAs. In Yates, Seneca, Schuyler and Ontario Counties, Riesling is the most planted wine grape, just ahead of Catawba.

united-states/high-valley.text: High Valley's east to west orientation is rare in the northern California Coast Ranges. The valley began as an east to west fault basin, and later volcanic activity, which built the Round Mountain cinder cone, closed it in and turned its drainage south into Clear Lake.

cite.name: T.D. TTB-30, Establishment of the High Valley Viticultural Area, 70 FR 37998 (July 1, 2005)

united-states/hudson-river-region.text: A southeastern New York AVA along the Hudson River. It takes in all of Columbia, Dutchess and Putnam Counties and parts of five others.

united-states/kelsey-bench-lake-county.text: A Lake County AVA on the bench lands just south of the Big Valley District, within the Clear Lake AVA.

cite.name: TTB Notice No. 134, Proposed Establishment of the Big Valley District-Lake County and Kelsey Bench-Lake County Viticultural Areas, 78 FR 20544 (April 5, 2013), adopted by T.D. TTB-118

united-states/lake-erie.text: A multi-state AVA along Lake Erie's southern shore across New York, Pennsylvania and Ohio. It includes the Chautauqua-Erie Grape Belt and holds Grand River Valley and Isle St. George.

united-states/laurelwood-district.text: A Willamette Valley AVA at the northern end, west of Portland and entirely inside Chehalem Mountains. Its distinguishing feature is the near-uniform Laurelwood soil, windblown loess over basalt.

cite.name: T.D. TTB-160, Establishment of the Tualatin Hills and Laurelwood District Viticultural Areas, 85 FR 34095 (June 3, 2020)

united-states/livermore-valley.text: An AVA in Alameda and Contra Costa counties centered on the city of Livermore in the Tri-Valley, inside the San Francisco Bay and Central Coast AVAs. Robert Livermore, a 19th century landowner, planted its first commercial grapevines.

united-states/long-valley-lake-county.text: A California AVA in eastern Lake County, east of Clear Lake, made up of a long, narrow valley floor and its foothills.

cite.name: T.D. TTB-188, Establishment of the Long Valley-Lake County Viticultural Area, 88 FR 42878 (July 5, 2023)

united-states/los-olivos-district.text: A Santa Ynez Valley AVA in Santa Barbara County, on a broad alluvial terrace plain of the Santa Ynez River, taking in Los Olivos, Ballard, Santa Ynez and Solvang.

cite.name: T.D. TTB-132, Establishment of the Los Olivos District Viticultural Area, 81 FR 3327 (Jan. 21, 2016)

united-states/lower-long-tom.text: A southern Willamette Valley AVA near Junction City and Monroe, west of the Long Tom River. Pinot Noir is its predominant grape.

united-states/madera.text: A San Joaquin Valley AVA in parts of Madera and Fresno counties.

united-states/mcdowell-valley.text: A small Mendocino County AVA near Hopland, a sheltered valley drained by McDowell Creek into the Russian River system. It sits inside Mendocino and the North Coast.

united-states/mcminnville.text: A Willamette Valley AVA in Yamhill County, where shallow silty clay and clay loam soils lie over marine sandstone and mudstone with intrusions of marine basalt.

cite.name: T.D. TTB-22, Establishment of the McMinnville Viticultural Area, 70 FR 2804 (Jan. 18, 2005)

united-states/mendocino.text: A Mendocino County AVA within the North Coast. Its sub-areas include Anderson Valley, Yorkville Highlands, Cole Ranch and McDowell Valley.

united-states/mendocino-county.text: A county appellation for wine from grapes grown mostly in Mendocino County, with two climate zones: a cool coastal west and an inland area mostly beyond the ocean's reach.

united-states/mendocino-ridge.text: A coastal AVA in Mendocino County made up only of ridge tops at or above 1,200 feet, roughly the fog line. Its boundary runs along the southern Mendocino coast from the Navarro River to the Sonoma County line.

cite.name: T.D. ATF-392, Mendocino Ridge Viticultural Area, Federal Register, 27 Oct 1997

united-states/moon-mountain-district-son.text: A mountainous Sonoma Valley AVA on the western slopes of the Mayacamas Mountains, where thin, well-drained soils come mostly from volcanic rock.

cite.name: TTB Notice No. 133, Proposed Establishment of the Moon Mountain District Sonoma County Viticultural Area, Federal Register, 4 Mar 2013

united-states/mt-veeder.text: A Napa Valley AVA high on the steep slopes of the southern Mayacamas Mountains, with shallow, mostly sedimentary soils. Its Cabernet Sauvignon is very high in tannin and acidity, capable of long aging, and often shows a distinct mintiness.

united-states/naches-heights.text: A small Columbia Valley AVA in Washington's Yakima County, on the western edge of the Columbia Basin. All its vineyards are farmed organically, biodynamically or Salmon-Safe, and its top grapes are Pinot Gris, Riesling, Gewürztraminer and Syrah.

united-states/new-york.text: A US wine state and the country's third-largest grape producer. American grapes such as Concord make up the largest share of its vineyards, ahead of hybrids and then vinifera. Its AVAs include the Finger Lakes and Long Island.

united-states/niagara-escarpment.text: A narrow New York AVA along a well-drained limestone ridge near Lake Ontario. It shares the lake and the escarpment with Canada's Niagara Peninsula.

cite.name: T.D. TTB-33, Establishment of the Niagara Escarpment Viticultural Area, 70 FR 53300, 8 Sep 2005

united-states/north-coast.text: A huge California AVA covering six counties north of San Francisco: Lake, Marin, Mendocino, Napa, Sonoma and Solano. Pacific fog and breezes shape the weather in much of it, but its sub-appellations range from cool to warm.

united-states/north-fork.text: A Long Island AVA on the North Fork peninsula, with a maritime climate moderated by Long Island Sound and Peconic Bay.

wiki.title: North Fork of Long Island AVA

united-states/north-yuba.text: A tiny Sierra Foothills AVA in Yuba County, California, with vines on terraced hillsides of granite and volcanic soils. Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah and Zinfandel are among the grapes planted there.

united-states/oak-knoll-district.text: A Napa Valley AVA at the southern end of the valley, near San Pablo Bay, whose maritime influence makes it one of the coolest parts of Napa outside Carneros.

wiki.title: Oak Knoll District of Napa Valley AVA

cite.name: T.D. TTB-9, Oak Knoll District of Napa Valley Viticultural Area, 69 FR 8562, 25 Feb 2004

united-states/oakville.text: A moderately warm AVA in the heart of Napa Valley, between the Vaca and Mayacamas Mountains, with gravelly alluvial loams on its western side and heavier volcanic soils to the east. Its main grapes are Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc, Merlot and Cabernet Franc, which give ripe, powerful wines.

united-states/oregon.text: A US wine state where Pinot Noir and Pinot Gris are the two most planted and most harvested grapes.

cite.name: Oregon Wine Board, 2025 Oregon Vineyard and Winery Census

united-states/paicines.text: A valley AVA in San Benito County, California, separated from Monterey County by the Gabilan Mountains. The San Benito River forms part of its boundary.

united-states/palos-verdes-peninsula.text: A California AVA on the Pacific coast of Los Angeles County, bordered by the ocean on the west and south. It takes in the cities of Palos Verdes Estates, Rolling Hills, Rolling Hills Estates and Rancho Palos Verdes, with about seven acres of commercial vineyards.

cite.name: TTB, Establishment of the Palos Verdes Peninsula Viticultural Area, final rule, 17 Jun 2021

united-states/paulsell-valley.text: A California AVA in Stanislaus County, in a valley carved by Dry Creek around the community of Paulsell. Its rolling hills rise above the flatter San Joaquin Valley floor to the west.

cite.name: TTB, Establishment of the Paulsell Valley Viticultural Area, final rule, 3 Jun 2022

united-states/petaluma-gap.text: An AVA in southern Sonoma and northern Marin counties, running from the Pacific Ocean to San Pablo Bay and lying mostly inside the Sonoma Coast AVA. Its low, rolling terrain lets cool marine wind and fog flow inland, strongest in the afternoon. The wind gives smaller, thicker-skinned grapes that need longer on the vine.

cite.name: TTB, Establishment of the Petaluma Gap Viticultural Area, final rule, 7 Dec 2017

united-states/pine-mountain-cloverdale-p.text: A small mountain AVA around Pine Mountain, about five miles north-northeast of Cloverdale, straddling the Mendocino and Sonoma county line. Its vineyards sit above 1,600 feet, higher than the fog that fills the valleys below.

cite.name: TTB, Establishment of the Pine Mountain-Cloverdale Peak Viticultural Area, final rule, 27 Oct 2011

united-states/potter-valley.text: A Mendocino County valley AVA, near the Eel River watershed. The valley floor lies at about 920 to 1,020 feet, ringed by mountains.

united-states/puget-sound.text: Washington's only AVA west of the Cascade Mountains, covering the lowland basin around Puget Sound in the state's northwest. Pinot Noir is the most planted grape.

cite.name: ATF, Puget Sound Viticultural Area, final rule T.D. ATF-368, 4 Oct 1995

united-states/ramona-valley.text: An AVA around the town of Ramona in central San Diego County, entirely within the South Coast AVA. A ring of hills and mountains encircles it, setting it above the lower coastal valleys to its south, west and north.

cite.name: TTB, Establishment of the Ramona Valley Viticultural Area, final rule, 7 Dec 2005

united-states/redwood-valley.text: A Mendocino County valley AVA north of Ukiah. It is cooler than the Ukiah Valley, and its grapes ripen and are picked later. In 1949 it held about half of the county's grape acreage.

cite.name: ATF, Redwood Valley Viticultural Area, final rule T.D. ATF-386, 23 Dec 1996

united-states/river-junction.text: A small AVA at the confluence of the San Joaquin and Stanislaus Rivers in southern San Joaquin County, on the western edge of the Central Valley. It is slightly cooler than nearby Modesto, Stockton and Tracy, and its soils hold an unusually high share of fine sandy loam for the area.

cite.name: TTB/ATF final rule T.D. ATF-452, River Junction Viticultural Area, 66 FR 23589 (9 May 2001)

united-states/rogue-valley.text: A large Southern Oregon AVA covering the Rogue River valley and its tributary valleys, such as the Applegate. Its eastern part is the warmest and driest, and Pinot Noir is its most planted grape, followed by Pinot Gris.

united-states/rutherford.text: A Napa Valley AVA in the center of the valley, known for its Cabernet Sauvignon. Its well-drained soils mix gravel, loam and sand with volcanic deposits and marine sediments.

united-states/san-antonio-valley.text: A warm, dry Central Coast AVA in the Santa Lucia Range of Monterey County, with Lake San Antonio in its southeastern corner.

cite.name: TTB final rule T.D. TTB-46, Establishment of the San Antonio Valley Viticultural Area, 71 FR 33239 (8 Jun 2006)

united-states/san-juan-creek.text: One of the easternmost districts inside the Paso Robles AVA, following the San Juan Creek valley at 980 to 1,600 feet. It sits in the rain shadow of the Santa Lucia Coast Range, so it is warmer and more continental than some of the districts to the west.

united-states/san-miguel-district.text: A district of the Paso Robles AVA around the town of San Miguel, with its northern boundary on the Monterey County line.

united-states/san-pasqual-valley.text: San Pasqual Valley was San Diego County's first AVA, approved in 1981, and sits within the South Coast AVA. It covers a narrow valley running inland from Escondido.

united-states/san-ysidro-district.text: An AVA in southern Santa Clara County, east of Gilroy, inside the Santa Clara Valley AVA. It is cooler than other parts of the valley, with breezes coming up the Pajaro River.

united-states/santa-margarita-ranch.text: The southernmost district of the Paso Robles AVA, ringing the town of Santa Margarita against the Santa Lucia Mountains and set apart from the other ten districts.

united-states/santa-ynez-valley.text: A Central Coast AVA in Santa Barbara County, in an east-west corridor between the Santa Ynez and San Rafael Mountains. It is very cool near the coast and warmer inland.

united-states/seneca-lake.text: A Finger Lakes AVA around Seneca Lake. The deep lake has not frozen over since the early 20th century, so it stores heat and lengthens the growing season. Riesling is the region's leading vinifera grape.

united-states/sierra-foothills.text: A large AVA in the Sierra Nevada foothills, across parts of eight counties from Yuba to Mariposa. Zinfandel is the main grape.

united-states/snipes-mountain.text: A small Washington AVA of about 4,145 acres near Outlook in the Yakima Valley, the state's third smallest. It holds some of the state's oldest vineyard plantings, and Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot are its top grapes.

united-states/solano-county-green-valley.text: A small North Coast valley AVA in Solano County, east of Napa Valley, about one mile wide and four miles long between the Vaca Mountains and the Mount George Range. Solano County is added to the name to tell it apart from Green Valley in Sonoma.

united-states/sonoma-county.text: Sonoma County's main grapes are Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Cabernet Sauvignon. It holds many AVAs, such as Russian River Valley, Alexander Valley and Dry Creek Valley.

united-states/sonoma-valley.text: A southeastern Sonoma County AVA, in the valley known as the Valley of the Moon. It contains the Moon Mountain District.

united-states/south-coast.text: A big Southern California AVA covering Orange County and parts of Riverside and San Diego counties, down to the Mexican border. Its sub-appellations share warm weather moderated by cool Pacific influences.

united-states/southern-oregon.text: An AVA in southwest Oregon that takes in the Rogue Valley and Umpqua Valley AVAs. Growers sought it as a name with more meaning to consumers, setting their wines apart from Willamette Valley wines. Pinot Noir is the most planted grape, followed by Pinot Gris, Syrah and Chardonnay.

cite.name: TTB, T.D. TTB-19, Establishment of the Southern Oregon Viticultural Area, 69 FR 70889, Dec. 8, 2004

united-states/sta-rita-hills.text: A Central Coast AVA in Santa Barbara County, in the western part of the Santa Ynez Valley AVA and entirely within it. Its name was shortened from Santa Rita Hills.

cite.name: TTB, Expansion of the Sta. Rita Hills Viticultural Area, T.D. TTB-141, 81 FR 56492 (Aug. 22, 2016)

united-states/stags-leap-district.text: A small Napa Valley AVA, only about one by three miles, noted for Cabernet Sauvignon. Soil sets it apart: loams from old Napa River sediment and volcanic soil eroded from the Vaca Mountains. A 1973 Cabernet Sauvignon from the district ranked first among the reds at the 1976 Judgment of Paris.

united-states/temecula-valley.text: A Riverside County AVA on the eastern slopes of the Santa Ana Mountains, inside the South Coast AVA.

united-states/the-hamptons.text: A Long Island AVA covering the South Fork, bounded by the Atlantic and Peconic Bay. Its growing season is cooler and foggier than the North Fork's, and its soils are mostly silt and loam.

united-states/the-rocks-district-of-milt.text: An Oregon AVA inside the Walla Walla Valley and the wider Columbia Valley, defined by its soil. About 96 percent of it lies on deep, cobbly Freewater series soils on an alluvial fan of the Walla Walla River, soils found only in tiny amounts elsewhere in the two larger AVAs.

wiki.title: The Rocks District of Milton-Freewater AVA

cite.name: TTB, Establishment of The Rocks District of Milton-Freewater Viticultural Area, T.D. TTB-127, 80 FR 6902 (Feb. 9, 2015)

united-states/tracy-hills.text: A California AVA south and southwest of the city of Tracy, on east-sloping land between the San Joaquin Valley floor and the Diablo Range. It lies in the rain shadow of Mt. Oso, which gives it a drier climate with less fog, dew and frost than the land around it.

cite.name: TTB, Establishment of the Tracy Hills Viticultural Area, T.D. TTB-54, 71 FR 65409 (Nov. 8, 2006)

united-states/trinity-lakes.text: An AVA in Trinity County in northwestern California, around two man-made lakes, Trinity Lake and Lewiston Lake, among steep timbered ridges and narrow valleys. The lakes cool the days and warm the nights.

united-states/upper-hudson.text: A large upstate New York AVA of about 1,500 square miles, in all or parts of seven counties including Albany. At the outset it had 19 vineyards on about 67.5 acres, planted to cold-hardy grapes such as Marquette, Frontenac, La Crescent and La Crosse.

cite.name: TTB, Establishment of the Upper Hudson Viticultural Area, T.D. TTB-152, 83 FR 62707 (Dec. 6, 2018)

united-states/washington.text: The second-largest wine-producing US state, with nearly all its vineyards in the dry eastern half, in the rain shadow of the Cascades, where about 6 to 8 inches of rain falls a year and summer days are long. Irrigation is key. Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot lead the red plantings.

cite.name: Washington State Wine Commission, WA Wine 101 (August 2026)

united-states/west-sonoma-coast.text: A Sonoma County AVA of 141,846 acres along the coast that contains the Fort Ross-Seaview AVA. Marine winds and fog shape its climate, and much of it lies in the cool Marine climate zone. When it was established in 2022 it had about 47 commercial vineyards on roughly 1,028 acres.

cite.name: T.D. TTB-179, Establishment of the West Sonoma Coast Viticultural Area, 87 FR 31180 (2022)

united-states/willamette-valley.text: Oregon's largest AVA, covering the Willamette River basin, with a cool climate of wet winters and dry summers and worldwide recognition for Pinot Noir. Pinot Noir is 72 percent of plantings, then Pinot Gris. A local Pinot Noir's top-ten finish against Burgundies at the 1979 Gault-Millau Wine Olympics first drew international attention to it.

united-states/willow-creek.text: A small California AVA of about 6,000 acres in Humboldt and Trinity counties, created in 1983. It is a narrow valley cut by the Trinity River in the Klamath Mountains and ringed by steep mountains.

cite.name: T.D. ATF-141, Establishment of Willow Creek Viticultural Area, 48 FR 37374 (1983)

united-states/yakima-valley.text: Washington's first AVA, set in a long east-west valley around the Yakima River and created in 1983. It holds more than a quarter of the state's planted vineyard acreage.

cite.name: Washington State Wine Commission, WA Wine 101 (August 2026)

united-states/yamhill-carlton.text: A Willamette Valley AVA in Oregon, around the towns of Carlton and Yamhill. It is a south-facing bowl of horseshoe-shaped, eroded hills.

cite.name: T.D. TTB-20, Establishment of the Yamhill-Carlton District Viticultural Area, 69 FR 71374 (2004)

united-states/york-mountain.text: A Central Coast AVA in California's San Luis Obispo County, west of Paso Robles. The York family established vineyards and a winery here in 1882.

cite.name: T.D. ATF-143, Establishment of York Mountain Viticultural Area, 48 FR 38462 (1983)

united-states/yorkville-highlands.text: A California AVA in southern Mendocino County along the Sonoma County line, between Anderson Valley to the northwest and Sonoma's Alexander Valley to the southeast. It was created in 1998 and sits inside the Mendocino and North Coast AVAs.

cite.name: T.D. ATF-397, Yorkville Highlands Viticultural Area, 63 FR 16904 (1998)

spain/condado-do-tea.text: A subzone of Rías Baixas, the Galician DO known for white wine from Albariño. A white labeled Rías Baixas Condado do Tea must be at least 70% Albariño and Treixadura.

cite.name: Rías Baixas DOP specification (pliego de condiciones), July 2024, Xunta de Galicia: the Condado do Tea subzone rule
